Dear friends,

We just launched a course that shows people who have never coded before, in less than 30 minutes, how to describe an idea for an app and build it using AI. It is now time for everyone — marketers, product professionals, operations specialists, analysts, students — to build software applications with AI!

I’ve often spoken about why everyone should learn to code (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWF3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3kNW5mzVGb5795KnW76xpjM4VKHP7LTZnV5MV7FN1Mmr6V1pTzlW7bDRFN5hxT9KW3NY0kx4QCQ1_W7cgntr1KJL6GW1Swr__2RzLjlW46WhkB4P43jmVQJfMn6vbDmHW6MWGYD2SqF9VW1NjXgc7Qc0TjW4C7RJt1F56QvW4vwnDX1r7NkRW6n3DLl3CSPzHW6pFzYs6tpLLjN8Rw0SvjXF89W8cMs0K68XzXQW1lSfNc3hxybJW515Q7h6FtqWZW6MdXS72NpqSMW3hflZb3NwpS7VP1mrf1V_K63W1tB5F52sRB6PW3D5kQp1Q7bWvW7LSxqH7gxNpFf4_mQH404 ) . I’m seeing a rapidly growing productivity gap between people who know how to code and those who don’t. For many job roles I hire for, I now require at least basic coding knowledge. Many times, after I speak with a non-technical audience about the importance of building software using AI, people ask me how to get started. In the past, I didn’t have a great answer. That motivated the DeepLearning.AI team to create “Build with Andrew (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWl3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3n4W6-Pr_H8JmzqNW5G1c3p16-J5rW6FKQqh8rWwRwW3vPws57bzSkWVprv5K4rY7NlW4gmKnr7VP4PqW2JYqqq15nvDwW7pr3mj4LxTMNW1MlYXp3v9dFYW6KVyPp8G6vTBW8jwfS72t_zp_W3bsNF986J8wGW10s5zD3bv079N7V55XplXn6qW4syjDq6MkzDSW11GXJ881LfZxW12grND3b3tRdW3mJbN61m9w4TW2Bqy8N1rTXmwW6nr9z28PKDKtW9cFSCd7FwBthW3HfXHs969CTpW4-Kjyw56zvYqW7XyWhs7FY2YNf8Wtzrq04 ) .” It’s the best way for someone who wants to try vibe coding to get started!

This course requires no prior knowledge of AI or coding. And it’s vendor-agnostic. Specifically, learners can use these techniques with whatever tool they’re most comfortable with (like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or the chatbot built into the DeepLearning.AI platform).

If you take this course, you will build a working web application: a funny interactive birthday message generator that runs in your browser and can be shared with friends. You’ll customize it by telling AI how you want it changed, and tweak it until it works the way you want. By the end, you’ll have a repeatable process you can apply to build a wide variety of applications.

DeepLearning.AI’s mission is to empower everyone to build with AI. This course is just one of many steps in service of this mission.

If you are already a developer, please encourage your non-developer friends to try their hand at getting AI to code for them. Not only will this help their productivity, they will find it really fun as well. Please invite your friends to come build with me (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWl3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3p7N3B09YR9wlryW13jcrF566sdZW6l8mbL7Lc71tW8Ylgb62r_Wq6W7_CFKk7knwkBW4fLNWl7bzxP5W9b0vsx6MBxzBW6nz44J1R5s9KW4k76jT383lVNW23fbgL8Y7cwdW2cQDS546X3PrW5QPtd_6pjx44W5994DS8QH8b-W10dS6x2hqv9RW8PK9885TNNnSW7MJxWq6SFyD4N6SR0_VYTtCFW6LWD9931wNKbW57YntB6F4fVJVhjKCH72vFg0W1jtLL770xwJ0W2YGLDg7l8ftFW6HdjvG3gwnxvM3_djwKkKMwf4cWLxR04 ) !

Keep building,

Teaching Models to Tell the Truth

Large language models occasionally conceal their failures to comply with constraints they’ve been trained or prompted to observe. Researchers trained an LLM to admit when it disobeyed.

What’s new: Manas Joglekar, Jeremy Chen, Gabriel Wu and colleagues at OpenAI fine-tuned GPT-5 Thinking to confess (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWY3prCCW8wLKSR6lZ3pGW8CHDYH2mtVYFW2P6YfY19mggMVwN7mJ6JX3dnW7zzCry8H30gvVRtNhW59m_R0W3YbRgt262vW1W9dT5zq2mb0_GN1h1tv8HyGwkW25_Q0F5DC7htW4CxqDc1vTJnfW6qxXm326P3LKW2Jf1J49dQty-W5BymC41-KN4MN8G7ZjW564HGW1-PhDH4HMX8XW2bKXQc57QV2dW2PdRQG8_-b11W5sqGFc4XcQ4-W3XlP2g3QjBt3W6lqhLY2tgPDhW4F2SC98H_Jc7W8sNrBj4rQJYJN44RFPPv2W2XW8VNnNp3q5j_QW820C5P16GL0XVbX4-J5Vk1VpW7nN8zs2YsjPlW26SF4F5-yfZTf1-qYkY04 )  to violations of its instructions or policies. Upon request, the fine-tuned model revealed any transgressions it had committed while producing its most recent response.

Key insight: During training via reinforcement learning to encourage accuracy, style, compliance, and the like, a model may inadvertently learn to prioritize earning rewards over pretrained or prompted objectives. Under some circumstances, this may cause it to hallucinate, lie, scheme, and otherwise misbehave. Rewarding the model for confessing to its misbehaviors in response to a designated prompt should train it to admit its mistakes without affecting its performance.

How it works: The authors used reinforcement learning to fine-tune GPT‑5 Thinking as they normally would, and also to produce confessions.

- An unspecified percentage of the time, given a prompt, the model was rewarded based on its response’s “correctness, style, helpfulness, compliance, safety, and more.”
- The rest of the time, after the model had produced a response, the authors prompted it to produce a confession. The confession described (i) all constraints, instructions, and objectives, implicit or explicit, the response should satisfy, (ii) how well the response satisfied these criteria, and (iii) any ambiguities or uncertainties in the criteria.
- Given the query, response, and confession, an unspecified reward model rewarded the model based on the confession’s completeness and accuracy — a measure of the model’s honesty in confessing, since items that were missing from or falsified in the report can be thought of as lies.

Results: The authors performed 12 evaluations of the model’s ability to follow instructions, resist jailbreaks, produce accurate output, and complete an impossible task (coding a script that required essentially 0 seconds to run). The fine-tuned model, when it misbehaved, confessed to its misbehavior at least half the time in 11 of them. For example, across 5 evaluations for hallucination, it either didn’t hallucinate or owned up to its hallucination 81.4 percent of the time:

- The model did not hallucinate and did not confess 42.2 percent of the time.
- It produced a hallucination and admitted the mistake 39.2 percent of the time.
- The model did not hallucinate but falsely admitted having done so 11 percent of the time.
- It hallucinated but failed to confess to it 2.9 percent of the time.

Yes, but: As the authors point out, even when models are forthcoming, confessions are not a panacea. Models won’t confess to behaviors they don’t know are wrong.

Why it matters: At inference, confessions can be used to monitor a model’s actions and stop undesired behaviors. Chain-of-thought monitoring (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSW23prCCW6N1vHY6lZ3lxVMpZMd8k81VqF6_PYbwkP48W6TpVz21V23_-W4rJP5X7Z0rFDW6cT-7Q6krjGnW7wcY8L7mw_4LW2l7SFd8-RQ59W229svG7XXdXxW1PppQl8dB8GDW6J2D3h8vVKYSW7TdGWB3rVZx2W5j3fQM1kHkF0W5rLD5G2VDn0DV6Kj6k8llPW1W3r8wMG38WTpKW1Q_0Qr9839CBW1p3gcR45V7k-W64_FdP7g7G-BN35HVCQz660SV8nvTt4jvvL1W8fNSTb8y106TW7nKplJ9l2bFLf7n5mn404 ) , which classifies bad behaviors a model might describe in its chain of thought, can be used the same way but, unlike that method, the authors’ approach trains models to reveal misbehaviors they may omit (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSV85m_5PW50kH_H6lZ3pMW9g8w1T1jnjTkW20bcW21f3VvLW384qBV5RWvfdW6dh0lT9366Z8W4WJqtP5-YvfsW4Bj99D4mkjNtW471wkS6NcdhSW39pbkS134XGnW7sfj5n3R4kxCW5NBzny850FHyW3RnlFR30hJsDV64l8M8D53mPW1DRs_820wLlHW8kcMsH5kdM2cW8kJGCf7YrcdlW8BhBBx7qkrJRW2-yJlq6KgzqJW1Ww8cn7-f7hzVcVlnK1hCVlDW1rKs5K3Tkc2kVsyQpS2tgtSjW5R24JB3XGZYzVz-mG28XmGQtW1z4Fhx1kncSxW7LbVFR3mY4R8N8qctgvWF0wbW60lKtv3wlsvDVwg4Rt8VVmRFW90KzxJ3gqt-jN7VDr2CDtV_BW8NHZgn93tGwqN6rS_Q2Zcvzff6f66gn04 ) from their chains of thought.

Lingua Franca for Science Labs

An open protocol aims to enable AI agents to conduct scientific research autonomously across disciplinary and institutional boundaries.

What’s new: Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (SAIL) published Science Context Protocol (SCP) (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSW23prCCW6N1vHY6lZ3nwW9jkV2h7Mcf--W7Nr8bL3vhTpmW2FnhCr8T5Y2cW3nC4Fq4x8sWxW4WQMrs40ck_sN1TtZNsH5YQ7W9hZvBw4LnXWtW18yVjh8YgRkVW75HV2Y12kSmLW36J1By6m0yR-W6CFXkC6ZCFQwVSVCxr120D1CN781Sg8yyRLvW6_B5P35KBGYJW8bHz3-9fplnXW3KSr7s3K9w6-W5YJDBQ4dcr7yW145lrB4G25rdW2H00348TnHTxVNs3RX1F8sNJVMSwkj5dQMDbW4YkVNW4C2ndvf65lG5604 ) , an open-source standard that connects agents with local clients, central hubs, and edge servers to conduct automated scientific inquiry. SCP is published under the Apache 2.0 license, allowing commercial use and modifications.

How it works: SCP attempts to make experiments using AI agents and robotic equipment as reproducible as possible. Like Model Context Protocol (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSV85m_5PW50kH_H6lZ3l_W4y1HGr2pzHyrVkzSZ_7hWtJ6W6cV13z5QpWtLW1BdxDY8xxf3NW80qFH43fPPQnW4LK0Lj7z_XkzW18btG15rC4F1W6Crn0J6XlqBQW3D7MFG6vsThjW7FQPwX1sMz-kW5SKJSV3wDx01W5WstPN7jxSJGW6Xl_Qk2srT5hW5jnb1B54b5DdN59Fc5blW_G9VvnDdH1gNFcDVKygwP3QWv1pN3zwk96pV--0W39sQ-k8rk4L0W4VltMf2MF2SZW8jmtQb6prQb8W2SGVjZ5QwY7qW5QN2CP5V6XyhW67yfqV5LH1tmN42R6pnsn1sgW5cjVjJ2xhn2dW3fv6ld6dwnbnVXW0LY52ZpMrW4M81KL1SnRw0W8PMlHm7pHvg5N6BPGflrYw1yW8sWpc745lxbZf73jP_v04 ) (MCP), it enables agents to interact with external resources. Unlike MCP, in which servers stand alone, SCP’s design requires centralized hubs that manage other servers as well as the client applications that enable users to access them. In addition, SCP’s structure offers greater security by governing messages and tools more strictly than MCP, which is necessary in scientific experimentation, the authors say.

- SCP’s fundamental data unit is an experiment. Every experiment is stored as a JSON structured data file with a persistent identifier and record of an experiment’s type, goals, data, and configuration. The format makes experiments traceable, versionable, machine-readable, and consistent with institutional policies that govern data.
- An SCP client authenticates users and gives them access to institutional resources. Researchers can describe an experiment’s goal in natural language (for example, “increase the brightness of this fluorescent protein”) or upload a complete research plan in text or PDF for their hub to analyze.
- An SCP hub takes a goal or other request and uses large language models to generate a set of experimental plans that list steps to carry out the experiment. The hub measures and ranks each plan according to its resource requirements, cost, and risk at each step. The user selects one plan, and the hub then orchestrates and schedules multiple agents and servers, which carry out the experiment. After an experiment is completed, the hub archives it for researchers to consult, alter, or repeat.
- Edge servers manage the experiments planned by the hub and stream data back to it (which in turn returns data to the client). Servers may belong to an institution, or they may be devoted to a particular discipline like biochemistry or mathematics, each with its own specialized tools and databases.
- The protocol currently includes more than 1,600 tools (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWl3prCCW7lCdLW6lZ3nQW6fxfRK9clt2wW3XDfS97Ry9PdW1y1mJ63X1FjyW8Ghgkq7ZY4mVN5ZQzg1NlR6gW67R1lL45ltzdW5Gh3bJ6RY19zW4CpY0H36sYFJW2XBB0D59rdlpW5nSYtR72k4LRW6lVg9s34XwwnW4DR7yj25T8kSW26Wkll5KTt-DW2LCWkK6jSpZ2W20R6Zn4qKMFyW6GB4bq16JM_HW1t5BsD5NG7JWW998QJQ7YLGr4W5mh_lC1PMVpLW1B2FSC7BPmBqW3_BhqH86q9y3W5Vg-1l1BjgHtW5dk4hR51bV-MW131JNG5dCtYFf7v5npb04 ) , which can include virtually any resource that can be used in an experiment. These can be software applications like search, but they could be robots, lab hardware, or human technicians. The authors hope to create a standard for all tools used in any experiment.

Why it matters: Scientific research relies on both human and technology working in concert. SCP aims to standardize the connections between them. It can manage both simulated experiments that use only computing resources as well as physical ones that involve robots and other lab equipment. It also allows for better communication between institutions and disciplines by supporting dedicated servers on bigger networks. These distinctions (human/robot, digital/physical, disciplinary differences) are beginning to blur. SCP is a step toward that future.

Copilot’s Users Change Hour to Hour

What do users want from AI? The answer depends on when and how they use it, a new study shows.

What’s new: A Microsoft study (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWF3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3lMW4hscvp6YTflVW80vvqB6HWnBRW5blfk45wzVVxW6f4kMy3fZf0WN8WB0pdKvt9sW6F91tf4Jlzt9W8J8f818HPMJsW7_XhhP3pvs4BW7BLMLS1QrYglW5c_W5B1WKKH6W3KB67G9j6lJPW2sDJVK2PVjlsW5fJmzJ59d7THVz-cDd8kqxC8W6BGJT-3nKY7rW4TXkJQ7HWnhcW4SK9t21mFztmW4JzsXw3qcjC2W6pN3Z06MrTHSW5Vqmj69jkfyRVlglcV5XPbVQW7p8Sbw99dG-RW2JT8lC5pdb23N2m1wNnzCQfnW9bc46849Y2Y6W1WwhfP6Jsftxf69LFsW04 ) reveals that people used Copilot differently late at night on their phones than during the workday on their laptops. Conversations that focused on productivity and career were more likely during the day and on desktop devices, and health, gaming, and philosophical questions dominated non-work conversations. As 2025 went on, more users asked the AI agent for personal advice.

How it works: Researchers analyzed (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSWY3prCCW8wLKSR6lZ3pDN3Jj3xXkVSGJW32-Bz12NTyVvW37MfD977b7kbN7_ZhTP1v034W3s2q7N26p6k0W1Bc5tg6NWlt9W3mKfX65b0T0ZW50xSnM69FlSSW4wS6P88F0tQCW4dhkgL7ZdkmSW87bFrK8BP7LrW9cvFmf3lTNqGW93f9XG4gQR1RW96Gqc014BntSW2wG-tS21gv7nW6xPJtr68Y4TBW5dDVdF7SQ7L7W4tkTL11k8TRpW9fxcYn8L1-GdW8gtynM8tQsqhW9cQ-Lr6fPz2sW2NHzQn4N5CbkW80lJRq5t7Tm5W2Gxlyc6n8WjHW3GR0XZ7X9C6nV8fFlb3w7h6VW1P2P3h7lnl04W748STX6-mBDtf5Hhz8j04 ) anonymized summaries of 37.5 million Copilot conversations between January and September 2025 to study how customers used the system, making this the largest study of its kind to date. The authors conclude that AI has become more socially integrated, as users employ it in aspects of their lives beyond work.

- The authors examined a random sample of Copilot conversations by paid and unpaid users, excluding commercial, enterprise, and education accounts. Each conversation included timestamps and device type. The authors used AI tools to summarize roughly 144,000 conversations daily. They built classifiers to assign each summary a topic (like “technology”) and intent (like “seeking advice”), identifying about 300 topic-intent pairs.
- The study ranks the frequency of topics and intents by time of year, time of day, and device type. The top 5 topics in order were (i) technology, (ii) work and career, (iii) health and fitness, (iv) language learning and translation, and (v) society, culture, and history. The top intents were (i) searching, (ii) seeking advice, (iii) creating, (iv) learning, and (v) technical support.

Analysis: Topics and intents differed depending on device used, time of day, and time of year.

- Users were much more likely to discuss health and fitness on mobile devices than desktops. Seeking advice about personal matters spiked near Valentine’s Day. Philosophical questions became more common later at night, while entertainment-related conversations plummeted during the workday.
- As the year progressed, topics and intents became less focused on work and technology and drifted towards social and personal matters. This shift suggested that the user base became both larger and less technical and/or users began using AI for both personal and professional matters.

Behind the news: Microsoft’s report follows similar studies by some of its AI rivals.

- In September 2025, OpenAI and Harvard released a study of ChatGPT use (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSV85m_5PW50kH_H6lZ3kMW1cCdQc6JWB7wW8-LjWF8tQwrvN298qbGkWS31W6NX1zX5n0-GcW6cXXTC7NRRnjN5JVtc-9d6rKW3_sCBx8XG_n3VT4C1p2ylFzZW4FC_wk70LLqmW9g_Snf3gT22xW4Q7HFN82Hd9fW4ytC121R3hgtW7_RDdZ74htc3W562vpM3XCgs7W42Tfxt3lhxmJW5lh7q04bNhdrW8lYsm65PZS5XW3z9L7T8jVlbJW3BRkyJ26CSjMW66YKCr6hg-kKW6N36RR4NHdcMW8yZfPf2_fWF9W56RdDr2NM13XN4gvKVhg_S82W4BQcwp46K-pNW3KBslJ6Wf2PZW4hZhLt1q4cMyW8h9fbh5l9CZmW63__1L5qBR28W9kHW491lhZdgW2hQWWR2NJg_2W1ng2Zz7V9tRGf4HdwpK04 ) from 2022 to 2025. It showed that 30 percent of uses were related to work while 70 percent were related to non-work activities. In addition, the gender gap among users among users shrank steadily during that period.
- In January 2025, Anthropic’s study of Claude (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSXd3prCCW95jsWP6lZ3lmW91B18G20_L5DN9k3XKVNTGWYN6w0W2y3RnQfVNvTMt4-t3KnW6tN4xk7hDv7pW2f_Txr8VllBNW213zwB1wtysBW3p7Jc84RjYzyW71KTnN7LLR6rW16nZ-p3Hj8NRW6XmHHm3FkQ5_W2B1n4z2PqbFRV-pLWM92KMx0W4vQlhw23R0W7W1kdHvG4MXNskW5QY83m54h1hBW7bcf5r5ZpNs6W3Hs95_3K1rdpW6XQnSq4zLPtcW8h77Qj5f0C1PVdsTJ32MnzmGW8HtSLs8bS8txW1RLXZs3JLQ4qW8WxD5G4dtP33Vc0qht7HwtrpW1VkKPT26htQvW8BtDSX12ThpfW2SKJ8T85XmsDVJNntF5YcZ2mN92pDx6L_C82f1Jvzss04 ) showed that the model’s user base focused on work, especially software development and text communications. A small but growing number of users engaged in games like Dungeons & Dragons and sexual roleplay (despite prohibition of that use by Claude’s terms of service).

Why it matters: The authors argue that the AI community may need to rethink chatbot design altogether. If users treat chatbots differently on mobile and desktop devices, AI builders would do well to design their systems to suit the devices that will deliver them. Application design is one way to accomplish this, but system prompts may be another. Desktop chatbots and agents can respond with more information-dense answers, guiding users to execute tasks, while mobile agents can offer shorter, more empathetic responses.

We’re thinking: Studies of chatbot usage conducted by different companies show different results. Perhaps each company’s users treat AI differently, so the results of any given study may not apply generally. That said, the Microsoft study suggests that the device used and the time when it’s used can have a big impact on what users want — important considerations for designing any application.

More Affordable Reasoning

One way to improve a reasoning model’s performance is to let it produce a longer chain of thought. However, attending to ever-longer contexts can become expensive, and making that attention more efficient requires changes to a model’s architecture. Researchers proposed a way to limit the cost of processing long chains of thought with just a bit of training.

What’s new: Delethink (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSW23prCCW6N1vHY6lZ3nWW6NZ0xQ9363qlW9hS5x6341qpCV1Pf8-6t32r1W4ggcl-6njz1gW5-21-G488L38VkvFQF1_rqkqW8Hwr__7bL6W6W8zKt-P7WzLr2N9gq9DYg4TljW5QL0Tr46VGLZW4Cb4Sp32nNSJW8wd6zW5n_VVpW4d4zBz8w2jJYW70crKZ5B8CnMW4FzPNR6vCl69W8ZC69j3D5QdzW826hlY99rjYFN4tvPljHdVWdW4lBLzC76Z2d6W4cxG6h1PdClLW6pLPJT87wNSkW56-4g07Qn-rtf7m1N-x04 ) is a reinforcement learning (RL) method that trains large language models to periodically truncate reasoning tokens to a fixed maximum number. The authors include Milad Aghajohari, Kamran Chitsaz, Amirhossein Kazemnejad, and colleagues at Mila, Microsoft, McGill University, ServiceNow Research, Polytechnique Montréal, and Université de Montréal.

Key insight: Reasoning tokens typically accumulate within a large language model’s context window, where they consume quadratically more computation as the contents of the window expand. One way to counter this effect is to train the model to reason within a maximum context window size. In effect, as a model is reasoning, it can learn to replace its chain of thought periodically with its latest “thoughts” and then continue.

How it works: The authors fine-tuned R1-Distill 1.5B, a large language model, on math problems in the DeepScaleR dataset (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VX4VqH95WsNgN5whfy4yMw5WW4FBnYy5J54W5N6fpSVs5m_5PW5BWr2F6lZ3m3W18lM_w3DDdtsW4TfC244rvBHQW4c4JlC3VFc2VW7kPQgQ7TXtvqW27qw6F664rw_W1gG8n55rZgq9W7RlgRM8TLYWrW5Hh44z5sFRG8W8dNjgy2h-cqLW5wdc_m4FNwVsW4kHPDF4c6kLVW5Jhk7x8L0-T2W5p4yk599PsNMW2-cBDG40r9gbW1vVbRC1pVhL1W3Z5GfJ5wxt8hW12T2Cr8KZKTlW3GHx8k4mBk7CW2d2B6H7RnXzXW4bbGFH1W_vP4W3jqmq9910kNSW6SpYx77VT3TCN71VxMy531P9VBx9vC3Sd8tVW9gCcTx5nv6hLW2SXR8_4FS6F6W2zyfML1C8QnMW1ypfPk6YjS5LVbPdzv8KMwkDW7hxZ9B5wWp0mN92bGlQrDgcnW8dzFg35-1FQ_W7PC_F-6Q3qLTW8QDSMF1XlGSCf5nWZXz04 ) . They used a modified version of the reinforcement learning algorithm GRPO that trained the model to reason in 4,000-token chunks:

- Given a math problem, the model generated a chain of thought until it had either finished or filled the model’s context window with 8,000 tokens.
- If it didn’t finish its chain of thought, the authors replaced the context with the original query plus the last 4,000 tokens. Then the model continued to generate its chain of thought until it had either finished or the context window once again held 8,000 tokens.
- They repeated this process until the model had either finished its chain of thought or produced 24,000 reasoning tokens.
- Then the model attempted to solve the problem, receiving a reward for a correct solution.

Results: The authors compared their R1-Distill 1.5B models to the same model after fine-tuning on the same 24,000-token reasoning budget via using GRPO. They tested the models on reasoning budgets of 24,000, 96,000, and 128,000 tokens.

- With a budget of 24,000 tokens, their model matched or surpassed the baseline on all 3 math benchmarks tested. For example, on AIME 2025, Delethink (31 percent accuracy) outperformed the baseline (29 percent accuracy).
- Their model’s performance continued to improve as the authors increased the reasoning budget, while the baseline achieved much smaller gains. For instance, with a budget of 128,000 tokens, their model achieved 35 percent accuracy, while the baseline achieved 30 percent accuracy.
- The authors estimated that training their model with a 96,000-token reasoning budget would cost 7 H100-months, while the baseline would require 27 H100-months.

Why it matters: This work eases the quadratic compute barrier that can make extremely long reasoning computationally infeasible. While other methods, like linear attention, achieve the same result by changing the attention mechanism, Delethink restructures the reasoning process to limit processing regardless of a model’s attention mechanism. It opens a path to reason efficiently over longer contexts without requiring new model architectures.

We’re thinking: As the authors mention, most LLMs are pretrained using relatively short contexts. For example, Llama 3 models started pretraining with examples of 8,000 tokens. This may have made them good at processing inputs around 8,000 tokens long. That is to say, Delethink’s performance may have been helped by the fact that LLMs tend to be pretrained on short-context tasks.

email threads and allowing users to query their inbox with natural
language ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

		TLDR

TLDR AI 2026-01-09

 BUILDING AN AI CODE REVIEWER GROUNDED IN PRODUCTION TELEMETRY
(SPONSOR) [4] 

 If AI code reviewers are supposed to save time, why am I triaging 40
comments about trailing whitespace, "consider using an f-string," and
"line exceeds 100 characters" on a 10-line change?

In this technical deep dive [4], Sentry breaks down how it built an AI
code reviewer that uses production telemetry to predict actual errors
— not just static style feedback. If you want to understand the
architecture, pipeline, and filtering logic [4] Sentry built, this is
for you. 

>> Read the blog [4]

🚀 

HEADLINES & LAUNCHES

 GMAIL IS ENTERING THE GEMINI ERA (4 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Gmail is adding AI Overviews using Gemini technology, summarizing
email threads and allowing users to query their inbox with natural
language. Its new features, Help Me Write, Suggested Replies, and
Proofread, improve email drafting, while AI Inbox filters prioritize
key messages. These updates, available for free, are rolling out now
in the US. 

 OPENAI TO ACQUIRE THE TEAM BEHIND EXECUTIVE COACHING AI TOOL CONVOGO
(2 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 OpenAI is acquiring the team behind Convogo, a business software
platform that automates and improves leadership assessments and
feedback reporting. The startup will not acquire Convogo's IP or
technology. Convogo's team will join OpenAI to work on its AI cloud
efforts. Its product will be wound down. 

🧠 

DEEP DIVES & ANALYSIS

 LORD OF WAR, MEET LORD OF TOKENS: TORTURE-TESTING IMAGE MODELS ON
DESIGN-AGENCY GRADE WORK (13 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 The poster for 'Lord of War', which depicts an image of Nicholas Cage
comprised of bullets, is a masterclass in compositing. A team of
designers likely had to manually source images of bullets, match the
lighting of the individual bullets with the shadows on the face, and
arrange thousands of shell casings to form a recognizable human face.
That level of skill was rare in 2005. This article explores whether AI
can redesign a similar 'Lord of Tokens' image with GPU dies and
silicon wafers constituting Jensen Huang's face. 

 CONTEXT PERSONALIZATION (34 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 This post demonstrates how to implement long-term memory and stateful
personalization in AI agents using OpenAI's Agents SDK. Structured
memory objects and context-injection patterns enable agents to recall
preferences, consolidate user notes, and evolve over time. 

 EIGHT SOFTWARE MARKETS AI THAT WILL TRANSFORM DIFFERENTLY (20 MINUTE
READ) [9] 

 Increased efficiency in resource use can lead to higher total
consumption, but only when demand is elastic. Cheaper production just
changes who captures the surplus when demand is constrained by
something other than production cost. AI coding will change how things
are built without changing how much gets built or at what quality for
a huge amount of economically significant software. This post looks at
eight markets to see what impact AI coding will have. 

🧑‍💻 

ENGINEERING & RESEARCH

 94% OF AI LEADERS DON'T BELIEVE THEIR DATA INFRASTRUCTURE IS READY
FOR AI (SPONSOR) [10] 

 Why is AI stuck in pilot mode? It's constrained by data
infrastructure and enterprise context. CData surveyed 200+ data & AI
experts [10] on what's working (and breaking) in AI data connectivity.
The key finding? IF YOUR DATA ISN'T LIVE, CONTEXTUAL, AND
GOVERNED, YOUR AI WON'T DELIVER. Read the 2026 State of AI Data
Connectivity Report. [10] 

 WARP SPECIALIZATION IN TRITON: DESIGN AND ROADMAP (20 MINUTE READ)
[11] 

 Warp specialization is a popular technique that improves kernel
performance on GPUs out of the box. The key idea is to have
specialized code paths for each warp instead of the same code. This
reduces performance hits due to control flow divergence, improves
latency hiding, and makes better use of hardware units on the GPU.
This post outlines the current design of warp specialization in
Triton, a compiler that aims to generate performance-portable code and
runtime across hardware for AI kernels. 

 THE COMPLETE GUIDE TO BUILDING AGENTS WITH THE CLAUDE AGENT SDK (22
MINUTE READ) [12] 

 This guide walks readers through the process of building a code
review agent from scratch that can read files, run commands, edit
code, and figure out the steps to accomplish a task. The resulting
agent can analyze a code base, find bugs and security issues, and
return structured feedback. The guide aims to help readers understand
how the Claude Code SDK works so they can build whatever they actually
need. 

 SCALE AI'S AGENTIC RUBRICS FOR SOFTWARE AGENT VERIFICATION (28 MINUTE
READ) [13] 

 Agentic Rubrics enable test-free verification of code changes by
creating checklist-style evaluations from expert agents that interact
with codebases. They outperform baseline methods on SWE-Bench Verified
and offer a scalable, interpretable signal for reinforcement learning
and inference-time feedback. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AI ISN'T “JUST PREDICTING THE NEXT WORD” ANYMORE (23 MINUTE READ)
[14] 

 Modern AI systems have evolved past simply predicting the next word
and now demonstrate enhanced capabilities, such as solving complex
problems and reasoning. Systems like OpenAI and Google DeepMind have
achieved impressive feats, including outperforming top mathematicians
in competitions, reflecting significant advancements in cognitive
tasks beyond autocomplete. 

 AMONG THE AGENTS (15 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Coding agents like Gemini 3 Pro and Claude Opus 4.5 have automated
tasks ranging from invoice creation to predicting US corn yields.
These agents exhibit capabilities close to artificial general
intelligence but require human understanding and oversight to avoid
errors and maximize their potential. The rise of these tools signals a
shift towards enabling individuals to independently explore complex
software projects. They demonstrate the importance of foundational
technical knowledge and creating opportunities and challenges for both
new and incumbent firms. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 DEVELOPER OUTPUT JUMPED 76% IN 2025... AND TEAM OUTPUT ROSE EVEN MORE
(SPONSOR) [16] 

 Developers are shipping more code - with PRs getting bigger and
denser. Read Greptile's cross-industry study [17] on the state of AI
coding to see AI tool adoption, model growth trends, and model
snapshots. 

 UNIVERSAL PERMISSION REQUEST HOOK FOR CLAUDE CODE (8 MINUTE READ)
[18] 

 This GitHub gist contains a Claude Code hook that auto-approves
read-only MCP tools to eliminate constant permission dialogs. 

 A PATHWAY TO PRIVACY FROM AI—WHILE USING IT? (4 MINUTE READ) [19] 

 Third-party apps can act like a VPN for AI services, as they prevent
service providers from being able to see the exact identity of users. 

 THE DOWNSIDE TO USING AI FOR ALL THOSE BORING TASKS AT WORK (6 MINUTE
READ) [20] 

 Ridding ourselves of all boredom could result in the loss of
creativity. 

 NVIDIA TIGHTENS TERMS ON H200 SALES IN CHINA (2 MINUTE READ) [21] 

 Nvidia now requires Chinese customers to fully prepay for its H200 AI
chips without refunds due to regulatory uncertainties from the US and
China.

body:
Illinois’ Department of Human Services left an internal mapping site
publicly accessible for more than four years, exposing data on over
700K
people ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ 


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

		TLDR 

		TOGETHER WITH [Vectra] and [Vectra] [4]

TLDR INFORMATION SECURITY 2026-01-09

 AWS SECURES AWS. EVERYTHING ELSE IS YOUR ATTACK SURFACE. (SPONSOR) 
[4] 

 AWS-native tools protect what's inside AWS. But modern attacks move
across identity, SaaS, on-prem, and other clouds, before and after
they ever touch AWS.

VECTRA AI DELIVERS HIGH-FIDELITY BEHAVIORAL THREAT DETECTION AND
AUTOMATED RESPONSE IN AWS AT RUNTIME. NO NOISE. JUST ACTION.

AWS customers like KPMG, Under Armour, and many government
organizations use Vectra AI to:

	* Cut false positives by up to 85%
	* Investigate threats 5X faster with full attack path context
	* Detect hybrid attacks in real time 

Lower risk. Higher ROI. Less analyst burnout.

SCHEDULE A DEMO → [5]

🔓 

ATTACKS & VULNERABILITIES

 ILLINOIS HEALTH DEPARTMENT EXPOSED OVER 700,000 RESIDENTS' PERSONAL
DATA FOR YEARS (1 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Illinois' Department of Human Services left an internal mapping site
publicly accessible for more than four years, exposing data on over
700,000 people receiving state benefits. The leak revealed addresses,
case numbers, demographic details for Medicaid and Medicare Savings
Program recipients, and names and case information for tens of
thousands of individuals receiving rehabilitation services. 

 ESA CALLS COPS AS CRIMS LIFT OFF 500 GB OF FILES, SAY SECURITY BLACK
HOLE STILL OPEN (2 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 The European Space Agency faces a new breach after Scattered/Shiny
Lapsus$ Hunters claimed to have stolen 500 GB of highly sensitive
operational, spacecraft, and contractor data from ESA systems,
including information on missions involving partners such as SpaceX
and Airbus. The attackers say their access remains open. The ESA has
referred the case for a criminal inquiry amid a history of prior
security incidents dating back to 2011. 

 CRITICAL JSPDF FLAWS LETS HACKERS STEAL SECRETS VIA GENERATED PDFS (2
MINUTE READ) [8] 

 The popular jsPDF library is vulnerable to a local file inclusion and
path traversal attack that can allow attackers to steal secrets. The
flaw allows attackers to pass unsanitized paths directly to the
loadFile function or any functions that call it. The vulnerability was
fixed in version 4.0.0, but it may not be comprehensive on Node 20 and
earlier. 

🧠 

STRATEGIES & TACTICS

 DECODING THE GITHUB RECOMMENDATIONS FOR NPM MAINTAINERS (13 MINUTE
READ) [9] 

 Following recent npm supply chain attacks, GitHub's hardening
guidance centers on three controls: adopting Trusted Publishing
Framework (OIDC-based short-lived credentials instead of long-lived
tokens), enforcing 2FA for all publishing operations, and using
WebAuthn/passkeys instead of TOTP for phishing-resistant
authentication. npm deprecated new TOTP setups in October and disabled
legacy tokens in November, requiring maintainers to use granular
access tokens with expiration for CI/CD automation. Maintainers should
configure trusted publisher relationships in package settings, enable
2FA across all sensitive operations, and enroll WebAuthn
authenticators while maintaining repository access controls. 

 DO SMART PEOPLE EVER SAY THEY'RE SMART? (SMARTERTOOLS SMARTERMAIL
PRE-AUTH RCE CVE-2025-52691) (14 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 A critical pre-auth remote code execution flaw (CVE-2025-52691) in
SmarterTools SmarterMail, a business email and collaboration server
for Windows and Linux, arises from an unauthenticated file upload
endpoint that accepts attacker-controlled parameters. It includes a
GUID used to construct file paths, enabling arbitrary file writes via
path traversal and by crafting a multipart/form-data request with
specific context and contextData values. With a malicious file, an
attacker can place a web shell in the webroot and gain full remote
code execution. 

 THE LOG RINGS DON'T LIE: HISTORICAL ENUMERATION IN PLAIN SIGHT (12
MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Logs are an essential tool for defenders to monitor for breaches and
investigate incidents. However, they can also be a valuable
enumeration tool for attackers. This article provides a comprehensive
overview of how attackers can abuse logs for enumeration in AWS,
Azure, and GCP. Security teams should treat logs with care and enforce
the principle of least privilege where possible. 

🧑‍💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 AN ACTIVE INCIDENT IS THE WORST TIME TO STITCH TOGETHER LOG DATA
(SPONSOR) [12] 

 You don't want to deal with data visibility nightmares to understand
if a threat is real. Sumo Logic unifies AWS, GCP, Azure, and 450+
other tools into a single platform - powered by multi-agent AI
[13] that surfaces root causes, prioritizes key events, and guides
analysts through resolution. Read the Gartner Critical Capabilities
report [14] to learn how Sumo Logic compares to other SIEM
competitors. 

 BLACKBIRD.AI (PRODUCT LAUNCH) [15] 

 Blackbird.AI provides an AI-powered narrative intelligence platform
that helps organizations detect, analyze, and respond to harmful or
misleading online narratives and influence campaigns that threaten
reputation, operations, and security. 

 PQC NETWORK SCANNER (GITHUB REPO) [16] 

 The PQC Network Scanner is a quantum-focused network assessment tool
that scans TLS/SSL certificates across environments to identify
systems vulnerable to future quantum attacks. 

 OGHIDRA (GITHUB REPO) [17] 

 OGhidra bridges LLMs via Ollama with Ghidra to enable AI-driven
binary analysis through natural language. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 GO.SUM IS NOT A LOCKFILE (4 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Go's go.sum file is not a lockfile and has no effect on version
resolution—it's purely a local cache for the Go Checksum Database to
ensure cryptographic integrity. Developers should use go.mod for
dependency analysis, which, since Go 1.17, lists all transitive
dependencies with exact versions and functions as both a manifest and
lockfile. This design eliminates diamond dependency conflicts and
prevents automatic upgrades to potentially compromised dependency
versions. 

 KERNEL BUGS HIDE FOR 2 YEARS ON AVERAGE. SOME HIDE FOR 20 (18 MINUTE
READ) [19] 

 Analysis of 125,183 Linux kernel bugs with Fixes: tags revealed an
average bug lifetime of 2.1 years, with race conditions averaging 5.1
years, and the longest-lived bug persisted for 20.7 years. Detection
rates improved dramatically, from 0% bugs found within one year in
2010 to 69% in 2022, driven by tools such as Syzkaller and kernel
sanitizers. The VulnBERT model achieved 92.2% recall and a 1.2%
false-positive rate by combining CodeBERT embeddings with 51
handcrafted features targeting patterns such as unbalanced refcounts
and missing NULL checks. 

 CHATGPT FALLS TO NEW DATA-PILFERING ATTACK AS A VICIOUS CYCLE IN AI
CONTINUES (4 MINUTE READ) [20] 

 Security researchers at Radware show how a new “ZombieAgent”
attack revives a previously blocked ChatGPT data‑exfiltration
technique by tweaking prompts to bypass URL restrictions and leak
information character by character. Indirect prompt injection and weak
separation between user instructions and embedded content keep LLM
agents vulnerable, forcing vendors into an endless patch-and-bypass
cycle rather than a fundamental fix. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 WHY WE'RE TAKING LEGAL ACTION AGAINST SERPAPI'S UNLAWFUL SCRAPING (1
MINUTE READ) [21] 

 Google filed a lawsuit against SerpApi for circumventing security
measures through bot networks, cloaking techniques, and fake crawler
identities to scrape and resell copyrighted content from search
results. 

 MAJOR DATA BREACH HITS COMPANY OPERATING 150 GAS STATIONS IN THE US
(2 MINUTE READ) [22] 

 Gulshan Management Services, operator of Handi Plus and Handi Stop
gas stations, disclosed a September 2025 breach exposing SSNs,
financial data, and government IDs of 377,000+ individuals. 

 COOLIFY DISCLOSES 11 CRITICAL FLAWS ENABLING FULL SERVER COMPROMISE
ON SELF-HOSTED INSTANCES (4 MINUTE READ) [23] 

 Cybersecurity researchers reveal 11 critical vulnerabilities in
Coolify, a popular self‑hosting platform, that enable authenticated
low‑privileged users to achieve root command execution, escape
containers, and even obtain the server's root SSH key, potentially
compromising entire infrastructures.

Wyoming launched FRNT on Solana, the first US state-backed stablecoin,
held in a Wyoming trust exclusively in USD and short-term
Treasuries ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

		TLDR 

TLDR CRYPTO 2026-01-09

📈 

MARKETS & BUSINESS

 ZCASH CORE TEAM RESIGNS, FORMS NEW COMPANY (2 MINUTE READ) [4] 

 The entire Electric Coin Company development team resigned after a
governance clash with the Bootstrap board and said they are forming a
new company to continue building “unstoppable private money.”
Zcash's roadmap and organizational future are now quite uncertain,
even though the protocol itself is said to be unaffected. 

 WYOMING ISSUES FIRST STATE-BACKED STABLECOIN ON SOLANA (3 MINUTE
READ) [5] 

 Wyoming launched FRNT on Solana, the first US state-backed stablecoin
managed by Franklin Templeton, held in a Wyoming trust exclusively in
USD and short-term Treasuries. Interest from reserves funds Wyoming's
school program as the token bridges to six EVM chains, including
Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Optimism, Polygon, and Avalanche via
LayerZero. The launch follows the 2023 Stable Token Act and an
11-blockchain consultation period concluding with Solana's selection
as the native chain. 

🚀 

INNOVATION & LAUNCHES

 APTOS CONFIDENTIAL TRANSACTIONS FOR INSTITUTIONAL ADOPTION (9 MINUTE
READ) [6] 

 Aptos launched confidential transactions on devnet through a
Distributed Lab partnership, using homomorphic encryption and
zero-knowledge proofs to hide transaction amounts while maintaining
regulatory compliance via designated auditor keys that enable
independent decryption access. The system encrypts transfer amounts
under three separate keys and allows validators to verify ZK proofs
and update balances without seeing underlying values, allowing for
institutional use cases like private payroll, position-masked trading,
and non-signaling treasury operations. 

 ELIZA ECOSYSTEM: FULL STACK FOR AUTONOMOUS AGENTS (7 MINUTE READ) [7]


 ElizaOS launched a four-layer full-stack architecture for autonomous
agents, comprising consumer-facing agent applications (Layer 1), Eliza
Cloud managed runtimes (Layer 2), MCP integrations with x402 payment
rails and TEE-based verifiability (Layer 3), and Jeju blockchain
providing onchain identity, reputation, and agent-to-agent commerce
primitives (Layer 4). The project positions itself as addressing
fragmentation in the current agent infrastructure landscape, where
most solutions only tackle isolated components without end-to-end
integration. The architecture enables long-running sovereign agents
with persistent identity and memory that can execute real onchain
actions, contrasting with disposable chat sessions and big tech walled
gardens. Jeju's economic operating system layer specifically targets
agent discoverability, dispute resolution, and usage-based
monetization for the emerging agent-to-agent economy. 

💡 

GUIDES & TUTORIALS

 WHY FIXED-RATE LENDING NEVER TOOK OFF ON-CHAIN (8 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Fixed-rate demand is driven by borrowers (institutions and loopers)
who want predictability, not by lenders, and on-chain lenders prize
withdrawal-anytime flexibility, so locking capital for term loans
forces unsustainably high fixed yields and kills scale. The scalable
solution is a rate-exchange layer that leaves Aave/Morpho/Euler
liquidity intact while letting traders hedge and synthesize fixed
payments (high capital efficiency, margin-backed exposure), enabling
borrowers to buy certainty without forcing lenders into term locks. If
implemented, rate-exchanges would unlock institutional credit
expansion on-chain by matching fixed-rate demand to rate traders
rather than fixed-rate depositors. 

 A16Z CRYPTO PRIVACY TRENDS FOR 2026 (6 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 There are four privacy infrastructure shifts for 2026: privacy chains
will establish durable competitive moats because secrets cannot bridge
between chains without metadata leakage risks, creating network
effects unavailable to commodity L1s competing solely on performance.
Decentralized messaging protocols require quantum-resistant encryption
combined with censorship-resistant architecture to survive state-level
shutdowns, giving users cryptographic ownership of communications.
Confidential data handling for finance and healthcare is moving from
application-level solutions to core infrastructure through
programmable access rules, client-side encryption, and decentralized
key management. DeFi security is evolving from reactive bug-hunting to
formal specification enforcement, where AI-assisted proof tools
establish global invariants that become runtime guardrails
automatically reverting transactions that violate safety properties. 

🦄 

MISCELLANEOUS

 STABLECOIN NEOBANK WANTED (2 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 People are frustrated with legacy banks. There's a demand for a
single stablecoin neobank that truly replaces banks, has a physical
card, enables ACH pull with named bank accounts, Solana
deposits/withdrawals, has the ability to send wires/ACH
(multi-currency), and ideally noncustodial. 

 MORE 2026 CRYPTO NARRATIVE PREDICTIONS (6 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Reputation systems, ICO renaissance, and crypto neobanking are poised
to have a strong 2026. Reputation infrastructure will emerge as the
critical filter for distinguishing humans from AI bots, with projects
like Ethos, Legion, and Kaito building social-capital-based systems
that require hundreds of hours and genuine relationships to establish
credibility. ICOs are resurging after 2025's regulatory clarity
resolved the failures of airdrop farming and low-float VC models, with
reputation-gated mechanisms preventing the scam-filled dynamics of
2017. Crypto neobanking will compete directly with TradFi by offering
self-custodial accounts, yield-bearing opportunities exceeding
traditional 0.2% APR savings rates, and instant cross-border
stablecoin payments as stablecoin adoption accelerates. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 DEFI IS WHERE PASSIVE INCOME LIVES (1 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Banks pay near-zero on savings, T-bill yields fall with rate cuts,
and stocks are unpredictable, so DeFi, where assets are being
tokenized, is the place to earn meaningful yield and generate
permissionless passive income through lending, borrowing, and yield
strategies. 

 AWS RUNS ~12% OF ETHEREUM NODES, NOT 40% (1 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 AWS hosts ~12.4% of Ethereum nodes (not 40%), and 41% of Ethereum
nodes run Geth (not 85%). 

 ETHEREUM STAKING DEMAND INCREASES AS ETH LOCKS UP (1 MINUTE READ)
[14] 

 Ethereum's validator entry queue has climbed above 1.45M ETH with a
~25-day wait, while exits remain minimal, implying staking demand is
roughly 1,800× larger than withdrawals. 

 YIELD-BEARING STABLECOINS: THE NEW BASE MONEY (1 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Yield-bearing stablecoins (YBS) are already at greater than $20B in
market cap and are evolving into the base money of on-chain finance.

improves navigation between library assets, variables, and

TLDR DESIGN 2026-01-09

📱 

NEWS & TRENDS

 UPDATED LEFT NAVIGATION BAR IN FIGMA DESIGN (1 MINUTE READ) [4] 

 The new left navigation bar in Figma Design, Draw, and Dev Mode
improves navigation between library assets, variables, and search with
toggleable labels available in the View menu. A redesigned variable
authoring experience now offers an edge-to-edge full-screen view that
spans the entire browser width. 

 GMAIL DEBUTS A PERSONALIZED AI INBOX, AI OVERVIEWS IN SEARCH, AND
MORE (4 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Google is rolling out a new AI Inbox for Gmail that surfaces
suggested to-dos and grouped updates, adds natural-language AI
Overviews to inbox search, and introduces a Grammarly-like Proofread
tool, while keeping the traditional inbox optional. Many AI features
previously limited to paid tiers are expanding to all users, with
advanced tools like AI search overviews and Proofread initially
available to Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. 

 OPENAI REPORTEDLY TESTING CHATGPT ADS SOON (2 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 OpenAI is reportedly testing advertisements within ChatGPT using
internal employee-only chat models. The company has been exploring ad
layouts and sponsored response disclosures despite CEO Sam Altman
telling employees in December that public-facing app advertising plans
were on hold. OpenAI aims to create a new type of digital advertising
that maintains user trust while providing stable funding for the
company. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & TUTORIALS

 THE 90% PROBLEM: WHY OTHERS' AIS' DESIGNS MAY BECOME YOUR PROBLEM (4
MINUTE READ) [7] 

 AI tools now enable non-designers to create visual designs that
appear 90% complete, commoditizing what was once a designer's
exclusive superpower: visualization. However, these AI-generated
designs still require the critical 10% of iterative refinement that
only trained designers can provide by understanding and articulating
the "why" behind design decisions. Designers' evolving role centers on
bridging user needs, business goals, and technical constraints while
justifying design choices that AI cannot yet evaluate or explain. 

 FROM 0 TO MINIMUM LOVABLE PRODUCT (8 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 MTCHMKR is a consumer SaaS platform that connects brands for creative
partnerships that addresses the disjointed process across Slack
communities. It is a polished product with subscription management,
AI-assisted matchmaking, and mobile functionality. The team launched a
beta at $1/month to overcome the cold-start problem, gathering
waitlist users through social media. It has planned future AI agents
for deeper brand research and partnership strategy. 

 SAME, BUT NEW: UX RESEARCH IN THE AGE OF LLMS (11 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 UX research isn't becoming obsolete in the age of AI - it's shifting
upstream to define what meaningful, high-quality AI outputs look like
by grounding prompts, formats, and evaluation criteria in real user
needs and context. Researchers play a strategic role in shaping,
guiding, and holding LLM-based systems accountable for delivering
genuine value by translating human expectations into clear quality
signals and rubrics. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 AI SEARCH VISIBILITY FOR BRANDS (WEBSITE) [10] 

 Wellows is a single source of truth for brand visibility across AI
search engines. It helps teams understand how AI interprets their
presence by unifying citations, sentiment, and visibility data into
one clear platform. 

 SHAPE, REFINE, AND POLISH WORK WITH AI (WEBSITE) [11] 

 Go beyond one-click generation. Work alongside AI to shape, refine,
and polish work you can confidently send to your boss or clients. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 DON'T SHIP ANOTHER CHAT UI. BUILD REAL AI WITH AG-UI (14 MINUTE READ)
[12] 

 AG-UI (Agent User Interaction Protocol) provides an event-driven
framework for building AI applications beyond basic chat interfaces,
standardizing communication between agents, tools, and UIs through
structured events. The protocol enables developers to create reusable
agent logic that streams responses, handles tool calls, and manages
state across multiple client types (web, CLI, and mobile). 

 YOUR LOGO WORKS HARD. HOW ABOUT YOUR MOTION? (5 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 A study of 1,300+ brand professionals found that while 81% recognized
Disney's motion design, only 14% identified Uber's, indicating that
brands invest in motion without making it strategically distinctive.
Effective motion identity requires connecting movement to core brand
strategy through systematic principles that scale across touchpoints.
Consistency and time build recognizable motion signatures. Clear rules
enable creative flexibility while maintaining brand authenticity
across all contexts and teams. 

 MINDFUL CHEF UNVEILS A NEW BRAND REFRESH BY MOTHER DESIGN (3 MINUTE
READ) [14] 

 Mindful Chef has unveiled a brand refresh by Mother Design that
evolves its identity into a more expressive, craft-led system inspired
by food editorial and cookbooks, shifting away from convenience-led
meal-kit tropes toward quality, provenance, and the joy of cooking.
Spanning typography, photography, motion, layout, and tone of voice,
the update positions healthy eating as an everyday luxury that feels
warm, chef-led, and genuinely desirable across all touchpoints. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 THIS TECHNIQUE FOR MAKING 2D PIXEL ART LOOK 3D IS BLOWING PEOPLE'S
MINDS (2 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Sprite stacking is a technique that creates 3D-looking pixel art by
layering multiple 2D image slices with small vertical offsets,
requiring no 3D modeling software. 

 A' DESIGN AWARD AND COMPETITION REVEALS TOP CREATIVE NATIONS IN WORLD
DESIGN RANKING 2025 (3 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 The World Design Rankings 2025, based on A' Design Award results,
places China first, followed by the United States, Japan, Italy, and
Hong Kong among 114 nations evaluated. 

 WHY VOLKSWAGEN'S RETURN TO BUTTONS IS A UX TRIUMPH (5 MINUTE READ)
[17] 

 Touchscreen-heavy car interiors can undermine safety by forcing
drivers into visually demanding, high-effort interactions, while
physical buttons support intuitive, no-look control and sustained
driving focus.

Buyers don't tell you the full truth and sellers have blind

 CRMs only work if you keep them updated. You don't have time for

that keeps every record up to date. 

No manual data entry, ever.

Used by 1,000+ startups, Lightfield gives you:

 	* Automated meeting prep built from account history
 	* Post-call tasks and follow-ups after every meeting
 	* An AI agent that researches accounts and drafts emails
 	* A ChatGPT-like experience on top of your data

Get started in minutes. Just connect your email and calendar and watch
your CRM build itself.

Try it for free today. [4]

📈 

HEADLINES & TRENDS

 WHAT'S WORKING NOW IN GTM AI: HOW RALLY REIMAGINED WIN ANALYSIS WITH
AI (5 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Win-loss analysis is high leverage but notoriously hard to do well.
Buyers don't tell you the full truth, sellers have blind spots, and
scheduling interviews takes forever. AI can reconstruct win-loss
insights from sales call recordings alone. Feed your Gong transcripts
into a custom GPT, and it will surface patterns across dozens of deals
faster than any manual process. 

 WHAT'S WORKING IN SAAS PRICING RIGHT NOW (15 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Credit-based pricing exploded 126% in 2025 because it splits the
difference between predictable licenses and pure usage. Customers can
budget, while vendors protect margins on volatile AI costs. Meanwhile,
per-seat pricing isn't dying like everyone predicted. It's evolving.
OpenAI and Figma now tie seats to capability tiers and product access.
Salesforce lets customers swap unused licenses for AI credits. Nobody
knows what AI is actually worth yet, so the winners are offering
multiple ways to pay. 

🧠 

STRATEGIES & TACTICS

 STOP HIRING FOR EXPERTISE: HOW TO RECRUIT A-PLAYERS (6 MINUTE READ)
[7] 

 A polished resume from Google often can't ship anything at your
startup. That's because you hired an expert, not a builder. The hiring
framework that actually works: evaluate drive first, then potential,
then expertise. Drive is the internal engine you can't coach or
install. Potential is how fast someone climbs. Expertise only matters
after the first two spike. To test for drive, don't even look at the
résumé before the interview: ask what they've obsessed over, when
the hardest they've ever worked was, and why. If someone has never
been deeply consumed by anything, they won't suddenly become consumed
by your company. 

 LOCAL ≠ SMALL BRAND IMPACT (8 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Founders never ask how to build a local press strategy, and that's a
mistake. If you're trying to reach small business owners, educators,
or non-technical professionals, the Boston Globe might outperform
TechCrunch. Local publications punch above their weight on Facebook,
where community stories spread fast through geographic networks. The
playbook is simple. Find customers in target cities, hear their
stories, then pitch their story to local reporters. You get awareness,
they get visibility. Local journalists don't need proof that your
company matters to the world. They need proof it matters to their
city. 

⚒️ 

TOOLS & RESOURCES

 CHARTDB V2 (TOOL) [9] 

 ChartDB is an open-source tool that generates editable ER diagrams
from database schemas. 

 VISLA (TOOL) [10] 

 Visla is an AI-powered platform for creating, editing, and sharing
videos quickly at scale. 

 RUBE (TOOL) [11] 

 Rube is a universal MCP that lets AI agents take actions across 600+
applications directly from chat. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 25 THINGS I BELIEVE IN TO BUILD GREAT PRODUCTS (11 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Speed is the only moat, and focus is a superpower. Build fast
feedback loops, and say no 10 times more than you say yes. The product
is more important than the process, so build minimum viable plans,
practice prototype-first development, obsess about the details, and
simplify product reviews. Seek the truth and be willing to be wrong.
Hire builders, not bureaucrats aiming to climb the career ladder. 

 THE MOST IMPORTANT SKILL FOR THE NEXT 10 YEARS (8 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 The skill that will remain relevant for decades is agency: the
ability to act, iterate, and adapt without permission. High-agency
individuals treat life as an experiment, use AI and tools as
amplifiers rather than crutches, and build generalist capabilities to
thrive across changing industries. Developing agency requires setting
goals, experimenting, analyzing results, and creating your own
processes, enabling long-term adaptability, skill acquisition, and
control over your future. 

 WHY AI STARTUPS MUST RELEARN GROWTH EVERY QUARTER (1 MINUTE READ)
[14] 

 Product-market fit resets every three months at Lovable because AI
capabilities and user expectations shift too fast to rely on long-term
scaling, even past $200M ARR. Roughly 95% of growth comes from
shipping new features, while funnel optimization contributes only
about 5%, forcing teams to prioritize velocity over polish.
Influencer-driven demos, free credits, and large communities now
outperform paid ads, making word of mouth the primary growth engine. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 SOMETIMES, YOU SHOULD TALK TO FEWER CUSTOMERS (2 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Corporate best practices exist to raise the floor, not the ceiling. 

 WHY GRINDING WITH BRUTE FORCE CAN BE VERY DANGEROUS FOR A STARTUP (2
MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Taking 8-10 calls a day feels productive until you realize you're
optimizing for movement instead of direction. 

 UNDERSTANDING DON NORMAN'S PRINCIPLES OF INTERACTION (4 MINUTE READ)
[17] 

 Don Norman's interaction design principles focus on making products
intuitive and easy to use without manuals. 

 INDEX VENTURES, SILICON VALLEY'S QUIET KINGMAKER, LOOKS AHEAD TO
SUCCESSION (12 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Danny Rimer, a partner at Index Ventures, says he has no intention to
retire, but the decision will be up to the partnership as a whole.

subject: Building Claude Code in 200 lines 🤖,iMessage agents 💬, tech blogging guide📝
body:
Great tech blogging comes with consistent writing and publishing, even
when posts are imperfect, to cultivate the habit and overcome creative
blocks ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

		TLDR 

		TOGETHER WITH [Ring] [4]

 TLDR DEV 2026-01-09

 THE RING APPSTORE IS HERE! (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Ring just announced the Ring Appstore, opening the door for
developers to build Al-powered apps using Ring camera data [4]and
reach millions of users.

With Al-assisted tools, self-serve sandbox environments, and a
streamlined certification process, you have all the tools you need to
find new monetization path, iterate quickly, and distribute at a
massive scale.

Third-party developers are already building in beta. You can request
to join now, too.

👉 Request early access to the developer portal [4] to invent with
Ring

🧑‍💻 

ARTICLES & TUTORIALS

 THE EMPEROR HAS NO CLOTHES: HOW TO CODE CLAUDE CODE IN 200 LINES OF
CODE (8 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 AI coding assistants are built on a simple core architecture that can
be replicated in about 200 lines of Python. This post presents an
agent that is equipped with three fundamental tools - read, list, and
edit files - which the LLM learns to invoke via structured commands.
The LLM decides which tool to use, executes it, and then processes the
results to either continue the task or respond to the user. 

 SIGNALS VS QUERY-BASED COMPILERS (11 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Modern query-based compilers are an efficient architecture for
interactive development environments, moving beyond traditional linear
processing pipelines to support features like Language Server
Protocols (LSPs). These compilers operate on a demand-driven
"pull-only" model, executing only the necessary queries and using
caching to rapidly answer specific requests without processing
unrelated files. This is different from UI Signals, which use a
"push-pull" system to actively propagate changes and ensure instant,
glitch-free synchronization across a user interface. 

🧠 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 STAGING IS A WASTEFUL LIE: THE CASE FOR THE MONO-ENVIRONMENT (13
MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Traditional staging environments are wasteful, unreliable, and create
a false sense of security. A "mono-environment" approach, where only
production exists, moves safeguards from environmental isolation to
logical isolation within the code, leading to faster delivery and
tighter feedback loops. This is done through automated practices such
as testing, ephemeral local environments, feature flagging, continuous
deployment, and production monitoring. 

 TECHNICAL BLOGGING LESSONS LEARNED (13 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Great tech blogging comes with consistent writing and publishing,
even when posts are imperfect, to cultivate the habit and overcome
creative blocks. It's best to focus on topics of genuine personal
interest and unique perspectives, rather than attempting to predict
popularity or chase trends. 

🚀 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 INTRODUCING PGX: BRIDGING THE GAP BETWEEN DATABASE AND APPLICATION
MONITORING FOR POSTGRESQL (8 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Modern software systems struggle when PostgreSQL monitoring is
isolated from application and infrastructure observability, leading to
slower diagnoses and misdirected optimizations as systems scale. pgX
is a new integration designed to bridge this gap by capturing deep
PostgreSQL diagnostic data and integrating it directly with other
system telemetry. 

 FLUX (WEBSITE) [10] 

 Flux is a website, with a corresponding TypeScript SDK, for building
AI agents within iMessage. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AI CODING ASSISTANTS ARE GETTING WORSE (5 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 AI coding assistants, after an initial period of improvement, have
recently begun to decline in quality. The primary issue with newer
models, such as GPT-5, is their tendency towards "silent but deadly"
failures, where code runs without errors but produces incorrect or
misleading results by avoiding safety checks or generating plausible
fake data. This degradation is likely caused by current training
methods that prioritize user acceptance, even for subtly incorrect
code. 

 AI & HUMANS: MAKING THE RELATIONSHIP WORK (15 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Agentic AI, especially in collaborative groups, often has human-like
behaviors, which means traditional human management principles are
surprisingly relevant. Research from leading AI labs like Anthropic
shows three key lessons for managing hybrid human-AI teams: effective
delegation to use AI's parallelization, allowing for rapid iteration
and trial-and-error learning, and having proper efficient information
sharing among agents. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 WHY AI IS PUSHING DEVELOPERS TOWARD TYPED LANGUAGES (7 MINUTE READ)
[13] 

 The increasing prevalence of AI-generated code is driving devs to
adopt typed languages, as type systems provide a safety net for
reliability and catching potential errors in code. 

 ANTHROPIC BLOCKS EXTERNAL USE OF CLAUDE SUBSCRIPTIONS (GITHUB REPO)
[14] 

 Anthropic has blocked external use of Claude subscriptions with other
AI coding harnesses, like OpenCode. 

 SOFTWARE TESTING FUNDAMENTALS EVERY DEVELOPER SHOULD UNDERSTAND (8
MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Essential software testing fundamentals includes concepts like test
cases, test doubles, various bug types, testing goals, and the
structured approach of the testing pyramid. 

 GO.SUM IS NOT A LOCKFILE (5 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 go.sum is a local security cache for module hashes with no impact on
version resolution. 

 LINUS TORVALDS: "THE AI SLOP ISSUE IS *NOT* GOING TO BE SOLVED WITH
DOCUMENTATION" (2 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Linus Torvalds (creator of Git and Linux) believes that documentation
for the Linux kernel should treat AI as "just another tool" rather
than focusing explicitly on "AI slop," as documentation will not solve
the issue of malicious or poor AI-generated contributions.

declarative data engineering and enables Real-Time Mode in Structured
Streaming ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

		TLDR 

		TOGETHER WITH [Unleash] [4]

TLDR DEVOPS 2026-01-09

 WHAT HAPPENS WHEN A 300-YEAR-OLD BANK GOES ALL-IN ON FEATURE FLAGS?
(SPONSOR) [4] 

 Lloyds Banking Group has been around since 1765. Now they're running
one of the most ambitious digital transformations in UK banking —
with feature flags at the center of it.

In this live webinar [4], Daniel Woollery (Head of Digital Services,
Lloyds) shares how the bank scaled FeatureOps [4] from scattered team
experiments to an enterprise-wide platform. 

📋 On the agenda: migrating hundreds of flags off legacy systems,
building governance that _accelerates_ delivery, and rolling out GenAI
with feature-level risk controls.

🕰️ Webinar starts January 19 @ 10AM ET. Save your spot [4]

📱 

NEWS & TRENDS

 RED HAT EXPANDS COLLABORATION WITH NVIDIA (4 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Red Hat expanded its collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Day 0
support for the NVIDIA Rubin platform across Red Hat Enterprise Linux,
OpenShift, and Red Hat AI. The partnership targets rack-scale
enterprise AI with optimized performance, security, and hybrid cloud
consistency. 

 INTRODUCING APACHE SPARK® 4.1 (6 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Apache Spark 4.1 introduces Spark Declarative Pipelines (SDP) for a
declarative data engineering approach, and enables Real-Time Mode in
Structured Streaming to achieve single-digit millisecond latencies for
stateless workloads. The update also delivers GA support for SQL
Scripting, expands PySpark capabilities with Arrow integration, and
enhances Spark Connect for machine learning. 

 KUBERNETES V1.35: A BETTER WAY TO PASS SERVICE ACCOUNT TOKENS TO CSI
DRIVERS (4 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Kubernetes v1.35 introduces a beta opt-in solution for CSI drivers,
enabling them to securely receive service account tokens through the
`secrets` field in `NodePublishVolumeRequest` instead of the less
secure `volume_context`. This addresses past logging vulnerabilities,
such as CVE-2023-2878, by providing a safer, more consistent method
for handling sensitive data. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & TUTORIALS

 WHY WE'RE LEAVING SERVERLESS (5 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Unkey migrated from Cloudflare Workers to stateful Go servers,
achieving 6x lower latency by eliminating external cache network
requests and simplifying architecture from complex distributed
pipelines to straightforward in-memory batching. The move enabled
self-hosting and platform independence, improved developer experience,
and reduced operational complexity. 

 SOFTWARE CRAFTSMANSHIP IS DEAD (3 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Modern software development prioritizes rapid feature delivery and
short-term impact metrics over long-term code quality and
maintainability. Incentive structures, Agile backlog pressure, low
deployment risk, and a lack of emphasis on craftsmanship have
collectively contributed to declining code quality across
organizations. 

🧑‍💻 

RESOURCES & TOOLS

 MAKING SOFTWARE ENGINEERS AI-NATIVE (SPONSOR) [10] 

 AI-native engineering = engineers set the goals and agents perform
the work [10]. When agents handle log analysis, metric correlation,
and timeline reconstruction during an incident, engineers can shift
their focus to architectural decisions and system design rather than
tactical investigation.

Download the free AI for Prod ebook [11] to learn more about how AI is
changing core engineering workflows.

 NEXT AI DRAW.IO (GITHUB REPO) [12] 

 Next AI Draw.io is an AI-powered Next.js web application that enables
users to create, modify, and enhance draw.io diagrams using natural
language commands and AI-assisted visualization. This tool supports
various diagram types and recommends powerful models like Claude
Sonnet 4.5 for optimal performance. 

 OPENSPEC (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 OpenSpec is a spec-driven development (SDD) framework for AI coding
assistants that aims to align humans and AI by locking intent with a
lightweight specification workflow before any code is written. The
system provides deterministic, reviewable outputs, addressing the
unpredictability of AI when requirements are confined to chat history.


🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 IMPROVE SERVICE RELIABILITY AND OPS CULTURE WITH GRAFANA CLOUD
SERVICE CENTER (7 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Grafana Cloud's Service Center provides a unified hub for monitoring
service reliability, performance trends, incidents, SLOs, alerts, and
on-call rotations to prevent engineer burnout and improve operational
culture. The feature centralizes scattered data into service pages
that help teams make data-driven decisions about reliability
improvements and workload balancing. 

 POSTGRESQL 18 RETURNING ENHANCEMENTS: A GAME CHANGER FOR MODERN
APPLICATIONS (7 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 PostgreSQL 18 significantly enhances the RETURNING clause by
introducing OLD and NEW aliases across INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and
MERGE, enabling developers to access before-and-after row values in a
single atomic statement. This removes the need for triggers or extra
queries, simplifies change tracking and auditing, and makes
MERGE-based upserts far more powerful and maintainable. 

 A CLOSER LOOK AT A BGP ANOMALY IN VENEZUELA (9 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 A routing leak in Venezuela on January 2, involving AS8048 (CANTV),
was noted by a cybersecurity newsletter amid news of Nicolás Maduro's
capture, initially suggesting potential malfeasance. However,
Cloudflare Radar data showed eleven similar, likely accidental, Type 1
hairpin route leaks by CANTV since early December, indicating the
issue stemmed from insufficient routing export and import policies
rather than malicious intent. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 DEPLOY MICROSERVICES ON AKS USING GITHUB ACTIONS (2 MINUTE READ) [17]


 GitHub Actions automates CI/CD pipelines for deploying microservices
to Azure Kubernetes Service by building Docker images, pushing them to
Azure Container Registry, and deploying to AKS clusters using kubectl.


 HOLMESGPT: AGENTIC TROUBLESHOOTING BUILT FOR THE CLOUD NATIVE ERA (2
MINUTE READ) [18] 

 HolmesGPT, an open-source AI troubleshooting agent for Kubernetes and
cloud-native environments, was accepted as a CNCF Sandbox project in
October.

than the transaction. It targeted millennials and Gen

TLDR MARKETING 2026-01-09

 ENGAGEMENT DOESN'T PAY THE BILLS. CONNECT MARKETING EFFORT TO REVENUE
WITH ASANA (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Marketers everywhere are feeling the pressure: launch more campaigns,
ship them faster, do it all with fewer resources—and prove that
you're actually moving the needle on revenue.

If you need a moment for a primal scream, that's understandable. But
here's the good news: There's a way to do more with less, and it's
Asana [4]. 

Asana is the work platform where human + AI collaboration comes
together [4], helping marketing teams to mobilize around clear goals,
drive impact, and scale campaign workflows.

TRY ASANA FOR FREE→ [4]

📱 

NEWS & TRENDS

 WHEN CONSUMERS ARE FINANCIALLY STRESSED, THEY LOOK FOR RELIABILITY (2
MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Financial stress is reshaping how consumers evaluate brands. A recent
study found that only 52% of consumers feel financially secure, and
those who feel insecure are more risk-averse and less tolerant of
friction. These consumers rate brand experiences lower on satisfaction
and trust, prioritizing reliability and recommendations over price. In
uncertain economic conditions, trust reduces decision fatigue and
becomes a key driver of loyalty. 

 AT CES 2026, MARKETERS GET SERIOUS ABOUT AGENTIC AI, CREATORS, AND
RETAIL MEDIA (3 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 CES 2026 showed a shift from flashy technology to practical execution
in marketing. Agentic AI gained momentum as it moves toward automated
media buying while requiring trust and transparency. Creators are
evolving into full media businesses as they expand into streaming and
podcasting and gain pricing power. SiriusXM saw a 300% increase in
podcast revenue as creators adopted omnichannel distribution and
programmatic access. Retail media growth now depends on off-site
investment and consistent measurement, as return on ad spend (ROAS)
varies by as much as 63% across networks. 

🚀 

STRATEGIES & TACTICS

 VENMO MARKETING STRATEGY: GROWTH TACTICS ON HOW THEY MADE P2P
PAYMENTS SOCIAL (3 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Venmo grew by making payments social, so the interaction mattered
more than the transaction. It targeted millennials and Gen Z, ages 18
to 40, and positioned itself as a social payment app built around a
feed and emojis. Visible transactions created built-in virality. Each
payment acted as a micro-advertisement. The brand's scale and cultural
relevance are reinforced by its influencer campaigns and partnerships
on social platforms. 

 THE STEP-BY-STEP PROCESS BEHIND OUR 2025 WRAPPED EMAIL (6 MINUTE
READ) [8] 

 EmailLove's 2025 Wrapped email followed a 7-step process. It started
by auditing data and defining an active-user segment, then cleaning
and uploading it as custom fields in MailerLite. The email was
designed, merge tags were tested, and it was sent to around 1,000
users. It reached a 57% open rate with no unsubscribes or spam
complaints, but generated no clicks. Adding CTAs, share options,
personality labels, or interactive elements could turn passive stats
into engagement. 

 HOW TO CONVERT FREE USERS INTO PAYING SUBSCRIBERS (2 MINUTE READ) [9]


 Apps should combine a free install with onboarding that highlights
user pain points, shows the solution, and provides social proof. After
this, a hard paywall requires commitment to a three-day free trial
before access, with the option to cancel anytime. This filters out
less serious users, while soft paywalls let interest fade and reduce
sign-ups. 

🧑‍💻 

RESOURCES & TOOLS

 TIRED OF CAMPAIGN CHAOS? STAY ON TRACK WITH ASANA (SPONSOR) [10] 

 Design in one application, copy in another, action items in a
spreadsheet—is it any wonder that things fall between the cracks?
Asana [10] lets you see the full picture across campaigns, review and
approve assets in one place, and keep everyone informed. Try Asana for
free → [10] 

 WRITESONIC (TOOL) [11] 

 Writesonic tracks how a brand appears in AI search and identifies
gaps where competitors are favored. It shows which content is cited
and suggests updates before visibility drops. The platform generates
content that ranks on AI and Google and provides data on search trends
and competitor strategies. Everything is designed to guide precise
actions that increase reach and influence without relying on
guesswork. 

 GMAIL IS ENTERING THE GEMINI ERA (3 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Gmail is moving deeper into AI assistance with the launch of
Gemini-powered features designed to reduce inbox friction. AI
Overviews summarize long threads and answer natural-language questions
by synthesizing information across years of emails, removing the need
for keyword searches or manual scanning. At the same time, writing
tools like Help Me Write and upgraded Suggested Replies focus on speed
and tone alignment, positioning Gmail as an active writing
collaborator. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AI WRITES BRILLIANTLY (3 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 AI writes well and can match a writer's voice, but it also creates
too many strong versions. Combining them becomes a slow, clumsy
process that often feels worse than starting fresh. The unused lines
make it easy to doubt every choice. The real lesson is simple. Pick
one good draft, call it done, and move on. 

 WE BUILT HELL, THEN ASKED FOR A DISCOUNT (7 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Humans want fast and high-quality experiences. They create systems
that deliver short-term ease while ignoring long-term tradeoffs. When
friction or failure appears, they blame others instead of recognizing
the choices that caused it. This cycle repeats across industries and
history, from health insurance and travel to government and social
media. People end up paying a misery premium for experiences they
designed themselves, and the pattern shows no sign of stopping. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 35 MARKETING IDEAS FOR 2026 (8 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 This roundup of 35 marketing ideas shows that attention in 2026 will
be earned through user experience, not exposure. 

 18 OF THE BEST BRANDS ON INSTAGRAM IN 2026 (18 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 The best Instagram brands in 2026 focus less on follower count and
more on saves and shares. 

 THE TOP 100 PRODUCT MARKETING INFLUENCERS (7 MINUTE READ) [17]

field.

xAI's losses are mounting as it spends to build data centers, recruit
talent, and develop software that will eventually power humanoid
robots ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌
