		TLDR 

TLDR 2026-01-09

📱 

BIG TECH & STARTUPS

 MUSK'S XAI BURNS ALMOST $8 BILLION IN CASH, REVEALS OPTIMUS PLAN (6
MINUTE READ) [4] 

 xAI's losses are mounting as it spends to build data centers, recruit
talent, and develop software that will eventually power humanoid
robots. The company reported that it spent $7.8 billion in cash in the
first nine months of last year. Its revenue nearly doubled
quarter-over-quarter to $107 million for the three-month period ending
in September. xAI expects to do more deals soon to continue building
out its Colossus data center site in Memphis, Tennessee. 

 THE MAN WHO COULD BE APPLE'S NEXT CEO (11 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 John Ternus, Apple's head of hardware engineering, could be next in
line to replace Tim Cook as CEO if he steps aside. Ternus, who joined
Apple in 2001, is known for his attention to detail and knowledge of
Apple's vast supply network. Apple began accelerating planning for
Cook's succession last year after Cook told senior leaders he would
like to reduce his workload. Cook will likely become the chairman of
Apple's board should he step down as CEO. 

🚀 

SCIENCE & FUTURISTIC TECHNOLOGY

 FORMER GOOGLE CEO PLANS TO SINGLEHANDEDLY FUND A HUBBLE TELESCOPE
REPLACEMENT (6 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and his wife, Wendy, have announced
major investments in four telescope projects. Each of the telescopes
brings a new novel capability online. The most intriguing instrument
is a space-based telescope named Lazuli that is designed to be a more
capable and modern version of the Hubble Space Telescope. The
Schmidts' investment, estimated to be worth half a billion dollars,
has enormous potential to advance the study of astronomy and
astrophysics. 

 HOW DID TVS GET SO CHEAP? (12 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 TVs today are vastly cheaper than they were 25 years ago, even before
adjusting for inflation. The price per area-pixel has fallen by more
than 90%. It's not surprising that the cost of the technology
declined. Virtually all of the major mechanisms that can drive
efficiency improvements have occurred. 

💻 

PROGRAMMING, DESIGN & DATA SCIENCE

 LLM PREDICTIONS FOR 2026, SHARED WITH OXIDE AND FRIENDS (9 MINUTE
READ) [8] 

 This post shares predictions Simon Willison made on a recent podcast.
The predictions cover what he thinks will happen in the next 1, 3, and
6 years in the tech industry. There has never been so much uncertainty
about what's coming in the next year. The significant advances in
coding agents in just the last two months indicate that things will
change significantly, but it is unclear what those changes will be. 

 EARLY LOOK AT GROK BUILD, UPCOMING VIBE CODING AGENT FROM XAI (2
MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Grok Build is a coding agent from xAI that can be accessed both on
the web and through a CLI. It currently supports local agents, with
remote environment support marked as coming soon. There are options
for users to configure agents and custom environments. A video
previewing the feature is available in the article. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 CHINA WARNS AI STARTUPS SEEKING TO EMULATE META DEAL: NOT SO FAST (6
MINUTE READ) [10] 

 China is reviewing Meta's recent acquisition of AI startup Manus, a
warning to Chinese entrepreneurs interested in Silicon Valley riches.
The review is part of broader consideration by China on how it can
build fences around its AI know-how. The government is identifying
standout companies and technologies with the aim of adding those of
strategic importance to an export-control list. Manus' parent company
was set up by Chinese co-founders in China, but it moved its
headquarters to Singapore last year to expand its global user base. 

 AWS IN 2026: THE YEAR OF PROVING THEY STILL KNOW HOW TO OPERATE (11
MINUTE READ) [11] 

 AWS isn't dying - it isn't even struggling in any conventional sense.
However, its era of unchallenged dominance is over. The company is
navigating a transition that would challenge any organization. It has
made the right strategic moves, but its success will depend on whether
it can retain the people who know how to deliver. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 LOVE WHAT YOU DO (1 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 The key to longevity is learning to love the work and the life around
it. 

 MUSK, OPENAI LAWYERS TRADE BARBS AS LAWSUIT HEADS TO TRIAL (5 MINUTE
READ) [13] 

 Elon Musk's lawsuit alleges that OpenAI's leadership made knowingly
false assurances to Elon Musk about its charitable mission that they
never honored in favor of their personal self-enrichment. 

 GOOGLE ANNOUNCES AI OVERVIEWS IN GMAIL SEARCH, EXPERIMENTAL
AI-ORGANIZED INBOX (3 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Google is rolling out a new AI feature that will let AI Pro and Ultra
subscribers ask natural language questions about their email inboxes. 

 THE 1,000 COMMITS PROBLEM (4 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Anthropic recently shipped code that broke the entire CLI. 

 WHY AI IS PUSHING DEVELOPERS TOWARD TYPED LANGUAGES (5 MINUTE READ)
[16] 

 Type systems have become a common safety feature for developers
working with AI because static types ensure that code is more
trustworthy and more maintainable. 

 CREATORS SAY SPOTIFY PAYS UP TO TWICE AS MUCH AS YOUTUBE FOR VIDEO
PODCASTS (10 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Spotify's dynamic ads will let hosts resell ad slots forever to
maximize their inventory.

 AI judges your product before customers do. Strong product
explainability helps AI represent your product accurately, turning
context engineering into a real PM advantage.

 Corporate rituals raise the floor, not the ceiling. Top PMs create

over busywork.

 AI can get designs 90% of the way there, but designers make them
right. The future of design is not drawing first, but explaining why
the final solution works. 

 OBSERVATIONS OF LEADERSHIP (PART TWO) (12 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 Leadership at scale is less about control and more about timing,
curiosity, and navigating complexity. Real progress comes from
understanding systems, embracing friction, and updating mental models
when conditions are right. 

🧑‍💻

helps them work together, rather than solo. Miro is hosting Forrester
analyst J.P. Gownder on January 22 to break down the data from 500+ AI
deployments. Register now [11] 

 THE GROWTH META: HOW TO BUILD A WAITLIST (4 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Waitlists no longer signal hype. The best ones qualify intent,
activate fast, and prove who will actually pay. 

 CHARGING FOR ADVICE MADE MORE PEOPLE ASK, NOT FEWER (2 MINUTE READ)
[13] 

 Charging for advice increases demand by removing social friction.
Price and async access signal openness, making it easier to ask for
and give help. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 THE TEXT BOX ISN'T ENOUGH (2 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 AI text boxes are powerful, but not enough. Like GUIs did for PCs,
better interfaces will unlock AI's real potential for everyone. 

 THE COLD START PROBLEM (3 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Network-effect products fail when they launch without density. Start
with one small, self-sustaining network, then repeat and scale.

 CHATGPT HEALTH (6 MINUTE READ) [4] 

 OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Health, a new feature designed to
assist users with health and wellness by securely integrating their
medical information into a personalized ChatGPT experience. 

 OPENAI EARMARKS $50 BILLION FOR EMPLOYEE STOCK GRANT POOL (1 MINUTE
READ) [5] 

 OpenAI set aside an employee stock grant pool equivalent to 10% of
the company last fall, when it was valued at $500 billion. The startup
has already given $80 billion in vested equity. It is in preliminary
talks with some investors about raising funds at a valuation of around
$750 billion. 

 ANTHROPIC RAISING $10 BILLION AT $350 BILLION VALUE (3 MINUTE READ)
[6] 

 Anthropic plans to raise $10 billion at a valuation of $350 billion.
The funding round is expected to close in the coming weeks, and the
total amount of the deal could change. AI companies collected a record
$222 billion in funding last year. This year is slated to be a big
year for public offerings. 

🧠 

DEEP DIVES & ANALYSIS

 8 PLOTS THAT EXPLAIN THE STATE OF OPEN MODELS (6 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Chinese companies are making strong, open AI models that are applying
increasing pressure on the US AI economy. Dethroning Qwen in adoption
in 2026 looks impossible, but there are areas of opportunity. The US
could very well have the smartest open models again in 2026, even if
they're used far less across the ecosystem. This post contains 8 plots
that show the impact of Qwen, DeepSeek, Llama, GPT-OSS, Nemotron, and
other new entrants to the ecosystem. 

 CONTEXT IS THE NEXT DATA PLATFORM—AND WHY CONTEXT GRAPHS ARE KEY TO
UNDERSTANDING PROCESSES (9 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Context graphs shed light on how work really gets done in the
enterprise. AI agents are a major unlock with automation, but only if
their reasoning is grounded in the right enterprise context. It's not
enough to just understand the enterprise data, systems also need
relationship knowledge. Context graphs enable agents to learn and
automate distributed work by capturing processes and learning intent
over time. 

 RECURSIVE LANGUAGE MODELS AND CONTEXT FOLDING (28 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Recursive Language Model (RLM) is a flexible solution to long-context
limitations in LLM agents. RLMs avoid summarization by delegating
memory management to scripts and sub-models. 

🧑‍💻 

ENGINEERING & RESEARCH

 ARE AI TOOLS FOCUSING TOO MUCH ON INDIVIDUAL PRODUCTIVITY? (SPONSOR)
[10] 

 Most companies aren't getting the AI results they want. This
Forrester study [11] shows how an overemphasis on individual
productivity, instead of collaboration, could be the culprit. For a
look at how collaboration-first AI lives up to the hype, join the Miro
webinar on January 22nd. Register now. [10] 

 FINEPDFS: LIBERATING 3T OF THE FINEST TOKENS FROM PDFS (52 MINUTE
READ) [12] 

 PDFs have been largely ignored by the open source AI community,
despite being a source of high-quality data for pretraining. Hugging
Face has created a new pretraining dataset of more than 3T tokens
spanning over 1,000 languages extracted from PDFs. This post details
how the dataset was created. 

 OPEN GAMING FOUNDATION MODEL (GITHUB REPO) [13] 

 NitroGen is a generalist gaming agent trained on internet gameplay
videos capable of predicting controller actions from pixels and
adapting to unseen games through post-training. 

 VISUAL WEB AGENTS (29 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 WebGym is a large-scale environment with nearly 300,000 real-world
web tasks for training visual agents. It has a high-throughput RL
system that boosts training speed and a fine-tuned Qwen-3-VL that
outperforms GPT-4o and GPT-5-Thinking on unseen web navigation tasks. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 CONSUMER AI PREDICTIONS (4 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Screenless and always-on AI devices will fail, while mini-apps enable
UGC personal software and a US consumer super-app. By 2030, consumer
AI will split into a reliable task assistant and an AI companion,
performance marketing will collapse, and AI-generated virtual creators
will explode. The biggest win will go to whoever solves AI discovery
beyond chat and search. 

 BRENDAN FOODY ON TEACHING AI AND THE FUTURE OF KNOWLEDGE WORK (56
MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Brendan Foody, the youngest unicorn founder and CEO of Mercor, is
transforming AI training by hiring experts like poets and economists
to create evaluation frameworks for frontier models. Mercor pays top
talent to teach AI models that are rapidly improving in economically
valuable tasks. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 Making AI agents doesn't have to drag on. Read this eBook from
Algolia to see how you can deploy branded conversational AI agents
while meeting business-sensitive timelines. Get the PDF [17] 

 GOOGLE SUPPORTS GEMINI-POWERED AUDIO LESSONS (1 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Google now lets educators create podcast-style audio lessons using
Gemini in Google Classroom. 

 AI WILL COMPROMISE YOUR CYBERSECURITY POSTURE (22 MINUTE READ) [19] 

 The breakneck speed at which AI tools are being integrated into
existing systems and workflows without proper threat modeling,
testing, and security analysis is dangerous.

 AI agents and MCP servers enhance threat modeling by automating the
synthesis of organizational context, enabling security teams to map
threats, identify detection gaps, and target high-priority threats
efficiently.

body:
CVE-2026-0625, a critical command injection vulnerability in legacy
D-Link DSL routers' dnscfg.cgi endpoint, has been actively exploited
in the
wild ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ 


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

		TLDR 

		TOGETHER WITH [Material Security] [4]

TLDR INFORMATION SECURITY 2026-01-08

 PROTECT YOUR ENTIRE WORKSPACE FOR THE COST OF EMAIL SECURITY
(SPONSOR) [4] 

 Today's email security stops at the perimeter. Once an attacker slips
past your inbound detections, they have free reign over years of
sensitive emails, files, and internal comms.

Material [4] protects the email, files, and accounts that live in
Google Workspace and Microsoft 365, improving security outcomes and
boosting efficiency for the same cost of email security alone.

Once deployed, Material [4] ingests all of your settings, contents,
and logs and translates them into:

 	* Step-up authentication for sensitive content
 	* Blast radius visualization for accounts,
 	* The ability to detect and respond to threats and risk across the
cloud workspace.

The fastest-growing companies trust Material. Book a demo to find out
what Figma, Reddit, Doordash, Lyft, and many more already know. [4]

🔓 

ATTACKS & VULNERABILITIES

 ONGOING ATTACKS EXPLOITING CRITICAL RCE VULNERABILITY IN LEGACY
D-LINK DSL ROUTERS (5 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 CVE-2026-0625, a critical command injection vulnerability in legacy
D-Link DSL routers' dnscfg.cgi endpoint, has been actively exploited
in the wild since November 2025, targeting end-of-life models
including DSL-2740R, DSL-2640B, DSL-2780B, and DSL-526B. The
unauthenticated remote code execution flaw enables attackers to hijack
DNS settings without credentials, allowing them to redirect traffic
and persistently compromise all downstream devices behind the router.
Organizations must immediately retire affected unpatchable devices and
upgrade to actively supported models, as the vulnerability leverages
the same DNS configuration mechanism used in previous large-scale
DNSChanger campaigns. 

 INSURER PROSURA HIT BY CYBER DATA BREACH, CUSTOMERS CONTACTED BY
THREAT ACTOR (2 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Australian rental car insurance provider Prosura suffered a data
breach that impacted an undisclosed number of customers. The leaked
data may include names, email addresses, phone numbers, country of
residence, travel details, invoicing and pricing data, and policy
dates. The threat actor also directly contacted impacted customers,
alleging that the company has been ignoring them. 

 LEDGER CUSTOMERS IMPACTED BY THIRD-PARTY GLOBAL-E DATA BREACH (2
MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Ledger has informed some customers who made purchases on ledger.com
that their personal data was compromised as part of a breach impacting
the third-party payment processor Global-e. Ledger and Global-e have
confirmed that no financial information or wallet seed phrases were
leaked as part of this breach. Global-e is also notifying other
impacted companies that utilize its services. 

🧠 

STRATEGIES & TACTICS

 THE MAC MALWARE OF 2025 (35 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 The 2025 macOS threat landscape was characterized by a surge in
sophisticated infostealers and state-sponsored backdoors that
increasingly leverage "Malware-as-a-Service" models and social
engineering vectors such as "ClickFix" and fake job interviews.
Technical analysis reveals that attackers are bypassing Gatekeeper and
static analysis by utilizing signed or notarized binaries and
executing multi-stage payloads written in Go, Python, and AppleScript
directly in memory. To combat these evolving threats, security
professionals must move beyond static signatures to implement
behavioral monitoring of process, file, and network activity while
educating users on the dangers of executing terminal commands from
untrusted sources. 

 VIBE HACKING: PROXYING FLUTTER TRAFFIC ON ANDROID WITH CLAUDE (6
MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Cronometer's Android app uses Flutter's own TLS stack, which ignores
system proxies and bakes certificate pinning into libflutter.so,
making traditional MITM approaches fail. By combining Frida on a
rooted Pixel with custom hooks, it becomes possible to detect and
patch Flutter's TLS verification, observe DNS lookups and socket
connections, and then transparently redirect selected hosts through a
proxy like mitmproxy. Injecting an HTTP CONNECT tunnel at the syscall
level lets HTTPS traffic flow through the proxy without modifying the
APK. 

 ALL YOU NEED TO KNOW ABOUT JA3 & JA4 FINGERPRINTS (5 MINUTE READ)
[10] 

 JA3 and JA4 are both methods for building a client fingerprint from
the TLS Client Hello. JA4 adds functionality and human readability and
is harder for threat actors to change. Both fingerprints can be
effective in threat hunting or monitoring. 

🧑‍💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 DIASYMBOLVIEW (GITHUB REPO) [11] 

 DiaSymbolView is a tool for visually inspecting debug information
recorded in .pdb files. It relies on the MSDIA API and presents a
hierarchy of debug symbols and their 200+ properties. 

 LYNIS (GITHUB REPO) [12] 

 Lynis is a security auditing tool for Linux, macOS, and UNIX-based
systems. It helps with compliance testing (such as HIPAA, ISO27001,
and PCI DSS) and system hardening. It is agentless, with optional
installation. 

 OPTI (PRODUCT LAUNCH) [13] 

 Opti is an IAM platform that uses specialized LLMs to automate
identity governance, least-privilege decisions, and remediation across
enterprise environments. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AUTOMATED DATA POISONING PROPOSED AS A SOLUTION FOR AI THEFT THREAT
(5 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 AURA is a tool that injects plausible false data into AI knowledge
graphs, rendering stolen proprietary data useless while authorized
users maintain access through secret keys that filter out the poisoned
information. The technique degrades unauthorized systems' accuracy to
5.3% while maintaining 100% fidelity for legitimate users, with an
under 14% increase in query latency, though experts express skepticism
about data poisoning's effectiveness and note that the solution
doesn't prevent insider tampering with knowledge graphs. Security
professionals should recognize that AI systems face unique challenges
in detecting and recovering from compromised data, as poisoned
information can propagate through machine learning processes faster
than traditional database corruption. 

 KRAKENLABS RESEARCH HIGHLIGHTS 2025: THE SHIFTS THAT REDEFINED THE
THREAT LANDSCAPE (14 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 2025's threat landscape evolution was characterized by AI integration
into cybercrime workflows, industrialized Crimeware-as-a-Service
platforms like Olymp Loader and LabInstalls PPI distribution, and
Initial Access Brokers monetizing compromised edge devices, including
Belsen Group's sale of 15,000 FortiGate device accesses. The year
witnessed a decline in traditional carding fraud under regulatory
pressure, while threat actors shifted toward identity abuse and trust
exploitation, exemplified by attacks on Salesforce-hosted airline data
and on cryptocurrency platforms targeted for geopolitical impact
rather than financial gain. Analysis revealed the convergence of
ideological hacktivism with ransomware business models, including
pro-Palestinian actor zerodayx1's BQTLock RaaS offering and leaked
Black Basta chats that exposed operational dynamics, underscoring that
basic security failures and third-party risk management remain
decisive factors in organizational breach outcomes. 

 HACKERONE 'GHOSTED' ME FOR MONTHS OVER $8,500 BUG BOUNTY, SAYS
RESEARCHER (4 MINUTE READ). [16] 

 Security researcher Jakub Ciolek reported two high‑severity Argo CD
denial‑of‑service bugs through HackerOne's Internet Bug Bounty,
expecting about $8,500 after CVEs were assigned and patches shipped.
Instead, he faced months of silence despite repeated follow‑ups,
raising concerns about trust in crowdfunded bounty programs and the
impact of noisy, low‑quality, or AI‑generated reports on serious
submissions. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 QUANTUM STRUCTURED LIGHT COULD TRANSFORM SECURE COMMUNICATION AND
COMPUTING (3 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 International researchers demonstrated quantum structured light
techniques that pack significantly more information and security into
photons by engineering high-dimensional quantum states. 

 CYBERSECURITY FIRMS SECURED $14 BILLION IN FUNDING IN 2025: ANALYSIS
(3 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Cybersecurity vendors attracted nearly $14 billion across 392 funding
rounds in 2025, marking a 47% jump from 2024 and the strongest year
since the 2021 peak. 

 LACK OF MFA IS COMMON THREAD IN VAST CLOUD CREDENTIAL HEIST (3 MINUTE
READ) [19] 

 A threat actor called Zestix used common infostealers like RedLine,
Lumma, and Vidar to harvest long-lived credentials from infected
machines and log dumps, then logged into corporate ShareFile,
OwnCloud, and Nextcloud instances that lacked MFA.

Airwallex plans to invest around €200 million in the Netherlands
over five years, expanding its Amsterdam team and using the country as
a
hub ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

		TLDR 

TLDR FINTECH 2026-01-08

📱 

NEWS & TRENDS

 AIRWALLEX DOUBLES DOWN ON EUROPE WITH €200M NETHERLANDS INVESTMENT
(2 MINUTE READ) [4] 

 Airwallex plans to invest around €200 million in the Netherlands
over five years, expanding its Amsterdam team and using the country as
a hub for European growth as it shifts focus beyond Asia-Pacific. The
move follows recent funding rounds that valued the company at $8
billion and comes as Airwallex prepares for a potential IPO while
competing with players like Adyen, Mollie, and Bunq. 

 JPMORGAN CHASE TAKES OVER APPLE CARD FROM GOLDMAN SACHS (4 MINUTE
READ) [5] 

 JPMorgan Chase is stepping in as the new issuer of Apple Card,
replacing Goldman Sachs after years of reported losses and operational
friction tied to the consumer credit product. The transition hands
stewardship of the high-profile card, built with Apple Card, to the
largest US bank by assets, signaling confidence that scale and
payments infrastructure can make the partnership work. 

 US WILL BAN LARGE INSTITUTIONAL INVESTORS FROM BUYING SINGLE-FAMILY
HOMES, TRUMP SAYS (2 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 The US plans to prohibit large institutional buyers from purchasing
single-family homes as part of a broader push to improve housing
affordability. Donald Trump said the policy would target Wall
Street-style landlords that have expanded rapidly in residential real
estate, arguing they crowd out individual buyers and first-time
homeowners. If implemented, the move could reshape housing supply
dynamics, potentially easing competition for entry-level homes while
forcing institutional capital to shift toward other real estate
assets. 

🚀 

DEEP DIVES & REPORTS

 FROM CHAT TO CHECKOUT: HOW AI AGENTS ARE REWIRING FINANCIAL SERVICES
(5 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Partnerships between PayPal, OpenAI, and Stripe show how
conversational AI is moving beyond support into payments and commerce,
turning chat interfaces into full transaction channels and reshaping
how financial services reach users at scale. 

 DEALMAKERS SEE M&A MOMENTUM CARRYING INTO 2026 (3 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 A KPMG survey of 300 US corporate and private equity dealmakers shows
strong optimism for 2026, with roughly two-thirds expecting higher
deal volumes and nearly three-quarters anticipating better deal
quality. Expansion into new markets, core business growth, and
acquiring technology capabilities are the top drivers, while political
uncertainty and regulatory enforcement remain the biggest risks. 

 MONEY 20/20 EVERYTHING IS FINTECH 2026 PREDICTIONS (19 MINUTE
PODCAST) [9] 

 In this podcast, Money20/20's team outlines four themes shaping
fintech's next phase, led by AI dramatically speeding up product
development while largely preserving today's market winners, even as
small teams gain the power to build at near-enterprise scale. They
also point to Asia driving a new model of “community finance
orchestrators,” pairing AI infrastructure with local, human agents,
alongside tighter global regulation aimed at safer, more interoperable
payments across crypto, stablecoins, and tokenization. Finally, they
challenge whether ChatGPT will evolve into true Western financial
super apps, with questions around consumer trust, regulatory
readiness, and whether AI alone can change entrenched financial
behaviors. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & PRODUCTS

 MASTERCARD AND LOANPRO PARTNER TO LAUNCH ‘LOAN ON CARD' SOLUTION (4
MINUTE READ) [10] 

 A new installment lending model is set to give borrowers instant
access to loan funds through a card-based credential instead of
traditional bank transfers. Built on Mastercard's Installments Program
and powered by LoanPro's infrastructure, the solution lets consumers
and small businesses spend approved funds anywhere cards are accepted
while keeping fixed repayment terms. The move highlights how lenders
are modernizing disbursement and control as real-time, digital-first
borrowing becomes table stakes. 

 FISERV'S CLOVER EMBEDS FACE AND PALM-BASED PAYMENTS (2 MINUTE READ)
[11] 

 Fiserv's Clover point-of-sale business is working with biometrics
outfit Wink to integrate face and palm payments technology directly
into its platform. 

 STRIPE PARTNERS WITH CRYPTO.COM (2 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Crypto.com has teamed up with Stripe to let its users spend their
cryptocurrency holdings directly at online merchants without first
converting to fiat currency. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 KLARNA HIT WITH INVESTOR LAWSUIT OVER BNPL CREDIT RISK DISCLOSURES (2
MINUTE READ) [13] 

 Klarna faces a proposed class-action lawsuit alleging it understated
consumer credit risks in its IPO filings, leading to investor losses
after its stock fell post-listing. The complaint claims Klarna failed
to disclose that many customers were under financial stress, though
the company says the allegations lack merit and notes its loan
delinquency rate remains below 1%. 

 BANK OF AMERICA'S AI-DRIVEN FORECASTING TOOL SAVED CLIENTS 250K HOURS
IN 2025 (2 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Bank of America says its AI-powered cash-flow forecasting tool helped
corporate clients dramatically cut the time spent on manual financial
planning tasks last year. The system analyzes transaction data and
liquidity patterns to automate forecasts, freeing up finance teams to
focus on strategy rather than spreadsheets. 

 BRAZIL'S PICPAY APPLIES FOR US IPO (3 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Brazil-based fintech PicPay has filed a registration statement with
the US Securities and Exchange Commission to pursue an initial public
offering on the Nasdaq under the ticker PICS, marking its second
attempt at a US listing after withdrawing a 2021 IPO plan. The company
reported sharply improved financials, roughly $1.37 billion in
revenue, and a net profit for the first nine months of 2025. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 GOLDMAN TURNS BULLISH ON COINBASE, BUT WARNS 2026 WON'T BE EASY (3
MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Goldman Sachs upgraded COIN to Buy on confidence in Coinbase's
growing non-trading revenue and long-term optionality in areas like
custody, prediction markets, and tokenization, while cautioning that
intensifying competition, rate sensitivity, and regulatory uncertainty
could keep margins under pressure in 2026. 

 CRYPTO VCS EXPECT CAUTIOUS REBOUND IN 2026 FUNDING AS STABLECOINS
LEAD AND TOKEN SALES STAY SECONDARY (4 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Crypto investors expect a modest, disciplined recovery in 2026. 

 PAYPAL BOOSTS ADVERTISING PLATFORM WITH CROSS-MERCHANT PURCHASE DATA
(2 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 PayPal has strengthened its advertising platform with a new programme
that provides firms with a unique, cross-merchant view into real
shopper behaviour, campaign effectiveness, and data-driven
recommendations.

on January 4, driven primarily by real-world asset tokenization
adoption ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌

		TLDR 

TLDR CRYPTO 2026-01-08

📈 

MARKETS & BUSINESS

 MORGAN STANLEY FILES FOR BITCOIN AND SOLANA ETFS (4 MINUTE READ) [4] 

 Morgan Stanley filed with the SEC for a spot Bitcoin ETF and Solana
trust – a strategic shift from distributing third-party crypto
products to creating in-house vehicles as institutional demand
accelerates. Spot Bitcoin ETFs have grown to $123 billion in total net
assets (6.57% of BTC's market cap) with $1.1 billion in net inflows
year-to-date, while Solana trusts have surpassed $1 billion in assets
following nearly $800 million in cumulative inflows. The ETF business
economics are lucrative – BlackRock's Bitcoin ETFs became the firm's
top revenue source in November with nearly $100 billion in allocations
– and Morgan Stanley's ability to vertically integrate these
products through its massive wealth management arm, which opened
crypto access to clients in October, keeps management fees in-house
rather than paying competitors. 

 ETHEREUM NETWORK USAGE HITS RECORD HIGH (5 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Ethereum's 7-day average of daily transactions reached a record 2.023
million on January 4, driven primarily by accelerating real-world
asset tokenization adoption, yet prediction market data reveal traders
assign higher odds to gold hitting $5,000 than Ethereum reaching
$4,000. Despite the network usage milestone, ETH is trading at $3,240,
with analysts attributing the sentiment disconnect to short-term macro
uncertainty and liquidity conditions outweighing on-chain fundamentals
in price discovery. Analysts argue this represents a temporary
divergence, noting that Ethereum's long-term investment case remains
anchored in its DeFi and tokenized asset dominance and suggests that
increasing ETH absorption into RWAs and DeFi protocols will tighten
effective supply and support more durable price appreciation.
Prediction markets show 58% odds for ETH hitting $4,000 versus falling
to $2,500, up from 43% at the start of the year, indicating some
improving sentiment despite the current lag behind gold. 

🚀 

INNOVATION & LAUNCHES

 G*BOY: THE FASTEST-GROWING IP IN CRYPTO (4 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 G*BOY's "Animate” is a tool that allows community members to
convert static images into high-fidelity videos in seconds. It builds
on the project's AI toolkit, which has already generated over 130,000
character-consistent assets, with the community now producing 90% of
the brand's visual output. Web3 IP is broken because projects treat
supporters as passive consumers rather than empowering them with the
same creation tools as core teams. G*BOY is positioned as a
community-proliferated franchise where token holders own stake in a
democratized IP that can compete with billion-dollar media companies
for attention on platforms like X and TikTok. The launch bets on
video's dominance in the attention economy while embracing community
taste rather than fearing supporters will "mess up" the IP as
traditional brands do. 

 XRPL'S MPT MAKES TOKENIZATION PRODUCTION-READY (1 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 The XRPL Multi-Purpose Token (MPT) standard embeds institutional
controls at the protocol layer (rich metadata, issuer-defined
permissions, KYC/AML authorizations, transfer restrictions, freezing,
and clawbacks) to deliver deterministic settlement, low fees, and fast
finality. This enables compliant stablecoins, tokenized MMFs, RWAs,
escrowed collateral, and closed-loop loyalty systems as
production-grade financial infrastructure rather than experimental
smart-contract pilots. 

💡 

GUIDES & TUTORIALS

 TRANSPARENCY WHEN YOU WANT, PRIVACY WHEN YOU NEED IT (SPONSOR) [8] 

 The transparency of traditional blockchains forces a difficult
choice: utility or privacy. Midnight [8] empowers innovators to break
free from this limitation, to a place where privacy is not just a
feature, but foundational.

PRIVACY MATTERS. BREAK FREE WITH MIDNIGHT [8]

 ETHEREUM'S INSTITUTIONAL MOMENT HEADS INTO 2026 (10 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Ethereum has exited the experimentation phase and is becoming the
default blockchain for institutional tokenization, stablecoins, and
custom Layer 2 deployments, driven by regulatory clarity, proven
uptime, and deep liquidity. Major banks and asset managers, including
JPMorgan, BlackRock, Fidelity, and BNY Mellon, are already issuing
tokenized funds and financial products on Ethereum, while stablecoins
and L2s position it as core financial infrastructure. Looking ahead to
2026, tokenized assets, stablecoins, and ETH's price are forecasted to
grow 5x as Ethereum solidifies its role as “digital oil” and an
institutional-grade treasury asset. 

 AAVE V4: A FAIRER LENDING MODEL WITH RISK PREMIUM (7 MINUTE READ)
[10] 

 Aave V4 overhauls lending by adding a “Risk Premium” that prices
borrowing costs based on the quality of a user's collateral, fixing a
long-standing issue where risky and safe borrowers paid the same rates
in shared liquidity pools. The protocol assigns risk scores to
collateral, computes a position-level risk premium using only the
collateral actually needed to back the debt, and accrues that extra
cost gradually through interest rather than upfront fees. This design
makes borrowing fairer, improves capital efficiency in Aave's new
unified liquidity architecture, and aligns interest rates more closely
with the real risk each position introduces to the system. 

🦄 

MISCELLANEOUS

 CIRCLE'S USDC OUTPACES GROWTH OF TETHER'S USDT (5 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Circle's USDC stablecoin grew 73% to $75.12 billion in 2025,
significantly outpacing Tether's USDT growth of 36% to $186.6 billion
for the second consecutive year, driven by increasing institutional
demand for regulated digital dollars following the passage of the
GENUIS Act. USDC's regulatory compliance – including state money
transmission licenses, New York virtual currency licensing, and MiCA
framework adherence in Europe – has made it the preferred choice for
institutions like Visa, Mastercard, and BlackRock, while USDT remains
unregulated in the US and Europe. Despite USDC's faster growth
trajectory, the two stablecoins still command over 80% of the $312
billion total stablecoin market, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent
projecting the sector could reach $3.7 trillion by decade's end.
JPMorgan analysts noted that USDC's transparent reserve management and
regular audits make it more trustworthy among institutional investors
and regulated entities compared to competitors. 

 STABLECOIN “INTERCHANGE” IS A CATEGORY ERROR (5 MINUTE READ) [12]


 Proposals to limit stablecoin rewards to merchant transactions
misunderstand stablecoins by treating them like credit cards, even
though their economics are driven by yield on reserves, not
transaction fees. Restricting rewards to spending would effectively
tax holders by forcing them to transact just to access value generated
by their own balances, while funneling yield to intermediaries. Such a
policy would undermine the GENIUS Act's pro-innovation intent, push
users and businesses offshore, and weaken US leadership in stablecoins
by ignoring how the technology actually creates value. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 GRAYSCALE ETH STAKING ETF MAKES FIRST DISTRIBUTION (2 MINUTE READ)
[13] 

 Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF (ETHE) became the first ‘33 Act spot
crypto ETF to distribute staking rewards to shareholders, covering
rewards from October 6 to December 31. 

 SENATOR LUMMIS QUESTIONS DOJ BITCOIN LIQUIDATION (2 MINUTE READ) [14]


 Senator Lummis expressed concern that the DOJ appears to have
violated Trump's executive order directing forfeited bitcoin to be
preserved for the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.

 MSCI decided not to exclude Bitcoin and crypto treasury companies
from its indexes, allowing firms like MicroStrategy to remain in major
investment benchmarks. 

 TOKENIZED T-BILLS ARE BECOMING CORE DEFI INFRASTRUCTURE (2 MINUTE

 The market cap of tokenized US T-Bill funds has reached $7.5B, up 50x
since 2024, driven by yield-bearing, onchain money market funds backed
by US Treasuries that offer stability and real returns.

sensors, a technology that captures infrared and ultraviolet light
alongside visible colors to potentially improve color accuracy and
low-light performance, for future iPhones. However, similar
implementations in Huawei phones delivered underwhelming results, and
given Apple's early, non-committal interest, it's unlikely the feature
will reach consumer iPhones anytime soon. 

 APPLE DESIGNER BEHIND IPHONE AIR IS JOINING THE AI STARTUP HARK (1
MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Abidur Chowdhury, a former Apple designer who worked on the iPhone
Air, is joining AI startup Hark as head of design. Hark, founded and
self-funded with $100 million by Brett Adcock (who also runs robotics
startup Figure AI), has recruited 30 engineers from companies like
Google, Meta, and Amazon, aiming to reach 100 employees by mid-2026.
The startup is developing AI models with its first release planned for
summer 2026. 

 LEGO SMART BRICKS INTRODUCE A NEW WAY TO BUILD — AND THEY DON'T
REQUIRE SCREENS (3 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 The Lego Smart Play system introduces interactive Smart Bricks, Tags,
and Minifigures that respond with lights, sounds, and motion sensing
without requiring screens. Powered by a tiny custom chip and a secure
Bluetooth-based network, the system allows pieces to recognize nearby
tags and each other, enabling more dynamic, responsive play. Lego's
first Smart Play sets, revealed at CES 2026 and themed around Star
Wars, will launch on March 1 with animated builds like Luke's X-wing
and a larger throne room duel set. 

🚀

WORKS (7 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Most UX designers fail at job hunting because they apply to
mismatched roles using a "spray and pray" approach that no longer
works in today's competitive market. This article presents a
five-phase research system: audit readiness through tool fluency and
portfolio quality, target specific industries with tailored resumes,
research companies beyond job descriptions, strategically network, and
treat rejection as diagnostic data rather than personal judgment. By
filtering opportunities rigorously and iterating on feedback,
designers can turn their job search from a numbers game into a precise
matching system that increases hiring success. 

 UX AND PRODUCT DESIGNER'S CAREER PATHS (8 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Annual retrospectives and self-assessment tools help UX and product
designers clarify career goals beyond traditional management tracks.
The Mirror Model and career matrices identify strategic opportunities,
including sideways moves into specialized roles like AI experience
design or design-engineering translation. Designers should proactively
shape positions that amplify their strengths rather than fitting
predefined roles, focusing on human-centered work that AI cannot
replace. 

 WHAT YOUR UX CAREER'S FINGERPRINT REVEALS ABOUT REAL VALUE IN AN
AI-DRIVEN MARKET (7 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 As AI accelerates design execution, the real value of UX work
increasingly lies in human judgment and sensemaking: the upstream
effort of framing problems, reconciling constraints, and stabilising
direction before screens ever appear. This often-invisible work,
rarely named in job descriptions, is what enables coherent execution,
reduces costly reversals, and becomes even more critical as AI makes
output cheap but poor decisions more expensive.

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 HOW TO REDUCE FRICTION IN REMOTE USABILITY STUDIES THROUGH BETTER
ASSET COLLECTION (9 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 Remote usability testing frequently fails due to disorganized asset
preparation—scattered links, incomplete instructions, and mismatched
materials—rather than flawed design or complex tasks. Intentional
asset collection, including centralized storage, clear instructions,
standardized moderator preparation, and pilot testing, eliminates
friction and strengthens data quality. Key strategies involve creating
a single source of truth, writing unambiguous participant
instructions, anticipating technical variability, and selecting tools
that support rather than complicate workflows. 

 YOUNGER PEOPLE WANT GOOD DESIGN IN EVERY DRAWER (4 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Younger generations expect everyday homeware to deliver flawless
performance, express personality, and adapt to their fluid,
budget-conscious lifestyles shaped by hybrid work and frequent moves.
Well-designed objects provide emotional support and self-expression,
transforming homes into curated spaces that serve as both sanctuary
and social backdrop. Brands must create durable, adaptable products
with emotional clarity that ground people through life's constant
changes rather than just looking attractive on shelves. 

 DELL, HP, AND LENOVO HEADED IN THE OPPOSITE DIRECTION TO APPLE WITH
NEW LAPTOP DESIGNS (2 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Apple is expected to unveil a thinner, redesigned MacBook Pro later
this year, continuing its long-standing push for sleekness despite
past trade-offs like lost ports, limited upgradability, and the failed
butterfly keyboard. In contrast, PC makers such as Dell, HP, and
Lenovo are moving toward thicker, more repairable laptops that
prioritise longevity and user-replaceable components over extreme
thinness. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 WHY GEN Z ARTISTS ARE REDISCOVERING ANATOMY, GESTURE, AND PLEIN AIR
PAINTING IN 2026 (5 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 Gen Z artists are increasingly choosing traditional techniques like
charcoal drawing, plein air painting, and anatomy studies over purely
digital methods. 

 AIDIA STUDIO'S MESMERISING FORMS BLEND BIOPHILIA AND LOCAL CRAFT (3
MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Aidia Studio, founded in 2018 by Mexican-Polish couple Rolando
Rodríguez-Leal and Natalia Wrzask, creates architecture that merges
computational design with biophilic elements and sustainable
solutions. 

 THIS ARTIST FOUND HIS CALLING BY TAKING INSPIRATION FROM RETRO VIDEO
GAME COVERS (2 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 Aleksa Stajsic is a Serbian artist who transitioned from studying
architecture and working as a barber into illustration, drawing
inspiration from childhood video game cover art alongside art history
and contemporary influences.

 GOODBYE LOW TEST COVERAGE AND SLOW QA CYCLES (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Bugs sneak out when less than 80% of user flows are tested before
shipping. However, getting that kind of coverage (and staying there)
is hard and pricey for any team.

QA Wolf's [5] AI-native solution provides high-volume, high-speed test

They can get you:

 	* 80% automated E2E test coverage in weeks [6]—not years
 	* Unlimited parallel test runs [7]
 	* 24-hour maintenance and on-demand test creation
 	* Zero flakes, guaranteed

The benefit? No more manual E2E testing. No more slow QA cycles. No
more bugs reaching production.

With QA Wolf, Drata's team of engineers [8] achieved 4x more test
cases and 86% FASTER QA CYCLES.

Schedule a demo to learn more [9]

🧑‍💻 

ARTICLES & TUTORIALS

 HOW DEPENDABOT ACTUALLY WORKS (8 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 Dependabot-core is an open-source, stateless Ruby library responsible
for the mechanics of tracking and updating dependencies across
numerous package ecosystems. The full Dependabot service, including
scheduling, state tracking, and pull request coordination, is managed
by GitHub's proprietary infrastructure, making the service difficult
to replicate independently. The library itself is a massive and
complex codebase that often resorts to workarounds to handle
ecosystem-specific nuances. 

 4 CSS FEATURES EVERY FRONT-END DEVELOPER SHOULD KNOW IN 2026 (6
MINUTE READ) [11] 

 CSS recently shipped `sibling-index()` and `sibling-count()` for
creating staggered animations and other calculations based on an
element's position relative to its siblings. `@container
scroll-state()` is new and can be used for querying specific scroll
states like 'stuck' or 'snapped', and `text-box` for control over
typographic whitespace. `typed attr()` is an advanced function that
allows HTML attributes to be used in CSS with type checking and
fallbacks. 

 THE SAUNA ALGORITHM: SURVIVING ASYNCHRONY WITHOUT A CLOCK (4 MINUTE
READ) [12] 

 The Sauna Algorithm is a metaphor for reasoning about time and safety
in fully asynchronous systems without clocks. By anchoring an action
to the arrival and departure of another participant who enters after
you, it shows how causal relationships (happened-before) can bound
execution safely without measuring time. The idea maps directly to
distributed systems, where nodes rely on causality, rather than
synchronized clocks, to guarantee consistency and correct ordering. 

🧠 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 LMARENA IS A CANCER ON AI (5 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 LMArena is a popular online AI leaderboard that is a broken system
for evaluating AI models. The platform rewards superficial qualities
like verbosity, aggressive formatting, and emojis over factual
accuracy because users quickly vote based on aesthetics rather than
careful evaluation. These wrong incentives lead models to optimize for
"hallucination-plus-formatting." 

 AN EXPERIENCED C PROGRAMMER TRIES AI AGENTS (7 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 A veteran C programmer found that treating agents like skilled
interns is the best way to use them. He delegates specific, tedious
tasks while he himself focuses on high-level design, analysis, and
optimization. 

🚀 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 HEADLAMP (GITHUB REPO) [15] 

 Headlamp is an easy-to-use and extensible Kubernetes web UI. It
combines traditional resource viewing with advanced functionalities,
supporting both in-cluster deployment and local desktop use. It has
multi-cluster management, plugin capabilities, and RBAC-driven access
controls. 

 TOOL UI (WEBSITE) [16] 

 Tool UI is a React component framework that renders schema-validated
JSON outputs from tools as inline, assistant-anchored, and interactive
elements for conversation-native UIs within chat applications. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 THE CONTEXT IS THE WORK (WHAT THE DAY-TO-DAY LOOKS LIKE NOW) (13
MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Coding agents have made code generation inexpensive, shifting the
core challenge in engineering from writing code to properly defining
intent, constraints, and trade-offs. As a result, PR descriptions have
become even more important, as they need to communicate this context.
A good PR description includes executive intent, reviewer guidance,
and detailed provenance to effectively convey information to various
audiences. 

 KERNEL BUGS HIDE FOR 2 YEARS ON AVERAGE. SOME HIDE FOR 20 (17 MINUTE
READ) [18] 

 An analysis of over 125 thousand Linux kernel bugs over 20 years
revealed an average bug lifetime of 2.1 years, with some, like race
conditions, hiding for over five years before discovery. While newer
bugs are being found faster due to improved tooling, a backlog of
ancient bugs still exists. To address this, a new tool called VulnBERT
integrates neural pattern recognition with 51 handcrafted code
features to successfully predict bug-introducing commits with 92.2%
recall. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 Devs express grief and a sense of loss over AI increasingly writing
most of their code, as it diminishes the personal satisfaction and
value derived from years of mastering the coding craft. 

 AI WRITES CODE FASTER. YOUR JOB IS STILL TO PROVE IT WORKS (10 MINUTE
READ) [20] 

 AI makes code generation faster, but it shifts the bottleneck from
writing to proving its functionality, making human verification and
accountability needed for good code review. 

 I GOT PAID MINIMUM WAGE TO SOLVE AN IMPOSSIBLE PROBLEM (9 MINUTE
READ) [21] 

 Through over-optimizing a floor-sweeping task, a Computer Science
student realized that prioritizing technically correct but ill-chosen
metrics invariably results in practically useless or even detrimental
outcomes. 

 NOI (GITHUB REPO) [22] 

 Noi is a macOS/Windows application and browser extension that
improves productivity and reduces digital clutter through features
like AI chat prompt management, multi-window organization, and an
integrated terminal.

Try Asana for free→ [4]

NEWS & TRENDS

 AUDIO ADS BEAT YOUTUBE VIDEO ADS IN EFFECTIVENESS (6 MINUTE READ) [5]


 Audio podcast ads drive 18-25% more purchases than YouTube podcast
views. Listeners seek out content intentionally and form stronger
connections with hosts. Meanwhile, YouTube audiences are often passive
or multitasking. Audio-first formats create a more intimate and
persuasive experience. Studies show consumers respond with stronger
physiological engagement, including higher heart rate and skin
response compared with video. 

 LINKEDIN JOBS ON THE RISE 2026: THE 25 FASTEST-GROWING ROLES IN THE
US (16 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 US job growth is being driven by AI and advisory roles. More than 56%
of professionals plan to job hunt this year, while 76% say they feel
unprepared. The list shows strong growth in founders and independent
consultants, which shows a shift toward self-employment. Sales and
marketing also show up on the list in several places. The rankings are
based on LinkedIn data from January 1, 2023, to July 31, 2025, and
include insights on skills, locations, experience, and flexible work. 

🚀 

STRATEGIES & TACTICS

 WHEN TO SHOW VS HIDE PRICES (4 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Delaying price disclosure increases purchases for premium products
but reduces purchases for affordable or discounted items. Across 6
experiments, people were 21.1% more likely to buy an expensive
espresso machine when the price appeared after adding it to the cart.
People were 18.1% less likely to want a 30% off espresso machine when
the sale price appeared after a click. People were 11.4% less likely
to buy from a daily deal email when prices were hidden. 

 WHY YOUR FIRST 200 WORDS ARE CRUCIAL FOR AI SEARCH OPTIMIZATION (7
MINUTE READ) [8] 

 AI search systems now prioritize the first 200 words as the main
source of context and credibility. Engines such as Google's AI
Overviews and ChatGPT use the opening paragraph to define topic
relevance, author authority, and audience fit. Pages that open with
clear entities and purpose are 38% more likely to be cited. Effective
introductions state the subject and identify the source, enabling
accurate classification and reuse in generative search results. 

🧑‍💻 

RESOURCES & TOOLS

 WHAT DATA FROM 5,000+ REAL PROJECTS TELLS YOU ABOUT THE IMPACT OF
AI-POWERED CREATIVE (SPONSOR) [9] 

 Most AI advice is theoretical. This Superside report [9] isn't, with
real data from 5,000+ CREATIVE PROJECTS. It shows how the "early
movers" are achieving a 40% REDUCTION IN DESIGN TIME and 10X FASTER
video and photo production — with $4.5M saved. But even now, only 2%
of creative leaders have fully integrated AI. Learn how to bridge the
gap. [9] 

 HOW TO CREATE AN ENGAGING NEWSLETTER (WEBINAR) [10] 

 Learn how to build an internal newsletter people actually read. This
session covers content structures, smart timing, and ways to fix
content gaps. It also explains how to measure success beyond open
rates. It will take place on January 28 at 11 AM ET. 

 GOOGLE TO ALLOW PREDICTION MARKETS ADS UNDER STRICT RULES (1 MINUTE
READ) [11] 

 Google will start allowing US ads for prediction markets on January
21, but only for CFTC-regulated exchanges and certified brokers that
pass Google's compliance process. The move opens a new channel for a
small group of federally regulated players while keeping strict rules
in place for ads, products, and landing pages. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 MRBEAST, SVEDKA, RITZ, GRUBHUB, AND MORE EARLY SUPER BOWL TRENDS (3
MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Early Super Bowl 60 advertising trends hint at a mix of AI
experimentation, creator-led content, and brand reinvention. Svedka
plans the first fully AI-generated ad for the Big Game, while MrBeast
may take creative control of Salesforce's commercial. Other brands
like Dove, Grubhub, and Ritz are using the event to reintroduce
themselves with new positioning or consumer-driven storytelling.
Despite rising costs that exceed $8M, enthusiasm remains high among
fans, especially for celebrity-driven and humorous spots. 

 AMAZON'S AI SHOPPING TOOL SPARKS BACKLASH FROM ONLINE RETAILERS THAT
DIDN'T WANT WEBSITES SCRAPED (3 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 Amazon's AI shopping tools, including Shop Direct and “Buy for
Me”, face backlash from retailers whose products were listed without
consent. Some businesses received orders for items they didn't sell or
that were out of stock. Over 180 retailers on platforms like Shopify
and Squarespace reported that their products appeared on Amazon
without permission. Amazon says businesses can opt out and that the
tools drive incremental sales. 

 THE 30 BEST PIECES OF COMPANY BUILDING ADVICE WE HEARD IN 2025 (30
MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Effective company builders prioritize execution over theory, proving
the value of early customer insights, immersive founder involvement,
and scrappy GTM experiments. Founders were advised to stay close to
product development and validate value through reverse demos and
onboarding built like video games. Successful exits in vertical AI and
breakout revenue growth at companies like Clay and EvolutionIQ showed
that tailored sales, opinionated design, and ego-free iteration are
essential in today's market. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 THE EVOLUTION OF SOCIAL MEDIA IN 2026 (1 MINUTE VIDEO) [15] 

 Brands should act like TV networks by running distinct show accounts
that drive attention back to the main one. 

 NOBODY'S CLICKING ANYMORE (1 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 AI overviews cut clicks, so the priority is to become the trusted
answer people recall without visiting your site. 

 A RANDOM TOPGOLF MOMENT EXPOSED WHY SO MANY BRANDS FAIL ON SOCIAL
MEDIA (2 MINUTE READ) [17]

online.

or treatment. The data will make ChatGPT's responses more relevant by
grounding them in user data. ChatGPT Health will initially be made
available to a small group of test users. OpenAI will expand access in
the coming weeks. 

 THE WAYMO OJAI WILL SOON OFFER AUTONOMOUS RIDES AROUND THE US (3
MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Waymo is preparing to update its lineup with a new van built by
Chinese automaker Zeekr and a modified Hyundai Ioniq 5s. The vehicles
will be added to Waymo's growing operations this year, but the company
has yet to specify which cities will see them. The Zeekr vehicle will
be called the Waymo Ojai in the US. Zeekr will construct the body of
the van in China before shipping it to the US, where Waymo will fit
its software suite and array of sensors. The vehicle will not be
affected by US regulations aimed at preventing Chinese cars from being
sold to customers in the US. 

🚀 

SCIENCE & FUTURISTIC TECHNOLOGY

 INSIDE THE SUB-ZERO LAIR OF THE WORLD'S MOST POWERFUL COMPUTER (10
MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Quantum computing holds the key to winning the rest of the 21st
Century. Google's quantum AI lab in Santa Barbara contains Willow,
Google's latest quantum chip. Willow has settled the discussion about
whether quantum computers can do tasks that classical computers can't,
and it has also solved a benchmark problem in minutes that would have
taken the best computer in the world 10 septillion years. This article
gives readers a tour through the Santa Barbara lab and discusses the
state of quantum computing and the potential impacts it may have in
the future. 

 THE GOLDEN AGE OF VACCINE DEVELOPMENT (32 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 Vaccine technology has changed inconceivably in the 230 years since
the accidental discovery of the first vaccine. Many diseases that
plagued humanity are now mostly forgotten. It has become far easier
and faster to develop new vaccines, and they can be engineered to be
safer and more precise than ever before. With progress speeding up in
recent years, the golden age of vaccine development seems imminent. 

💻 

PROGRAMMING, DESIGN & DATA SCIENCE

 THE MODERN AI PM IN THE AGE OF AGENTS (10 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 The job of the PM used to be to translate what customers want into
specs that would be handed to engineers. That translation layer is
compressing. PMs are now writing specs for AI agents to implement. The
bottleneck has shifted upstream as the implementation barrier has
dropped. The scarce resource is now knowing what's actually worth
building. 

 AI'S IMPACT ON TAILWIND (2 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 75% of Tailwind's engineering team lost their jobs due to the impact
AI has had on the business. Traffic to Tailwind's docs is down about
40% from early 2023. The docs are the only way for people to discover
Tailwind's commercial products, so this is resulting in less income
for the project. While Tailwind is growing faster than ever and is
bigger than it has ever been, its revenue is down close to 80%. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 CONSUMER AI PREDICTIONS (5 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 Phones are too powerful - screenless AI devices will flop, as will
'always listening' devices. Mini-apps will unlock UGC personal
software. There will be two big general-purpose AI chatbots by 2030.
Performance marketing for apps is dead. The fastest consumer product
to reach $1 billion ARR will be an AI webcam girl. Whoever figures out
how to unlock use cases for AI beyond search and chat will be the next
big consumer platform. 

 MICROSOFT'S WOULD-HAVE-BEEN $30B "HACKQUISITION" OF OPENAI (6 MINUTE
READ) [11] 

 Microsoft's 'hackquisition' of Inflection in 2024 was groundbreaking
and led basically all of its rivals to copy the same general
structure. Microsoft first conceived the plan when Sam Altman was
ousted as CEO in November 2023. It had planned to hire the entire
company if OpenAI refused to reinstate Altman. Altman was quickly
reinstated, but the situation clearly planted the seed that would grow
into the 'hackquisition' model. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 STACK OVERFLOW'S FORUM IS DEAD THANKS TO AI, BUT THE COMPANY'S STILL
KICKING... THANKS TO AI (2 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Stack Overflow's revenue has roughly doubled to $115 million since
ChatGPT's 2022 debut. 

 AI WRITES CODE FASTER. YOUR JOB IS STILL TO PROVE IT WORKS (12 MINUTE
READ) [13] 

 Include evidence that your code works along with your pull requests
to ensure you are not moving work downstream. 

 WARNER BROS. STICKS WITH NETFLIX MERGER, CALLS PARAMOUNT'S $108B BID
“ILLUSORY” (10 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Paramount's offer would require an extraordinary amount of debt
financing and other terms that make it less likely to be completed
than a Netflix merger. 

 AWS AND MICROSOFT ARE SELLING MUCH MORE THAN CLOUD SERVICES (9 MINUTE
READ) [15] 

 To compete with the large cloud providers, you need to make
businesses 100% comfortable with doing business with you. 

 CLAUDE CODE AND WHAT COMES NEXT (15 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 AIs are now capable of real, sustained work that actually matters,
and this is starting to change how developers approach tasks. 

 ADVANCEMENTS IN SELF-DRIVING CARS (28 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Self-driving cars will change quite a lot wherever the technology is
allowed to proceed.

📱 

DEEP DIVES

 MIGRATION AT SCALE: MOVING MARKETING CLOUD CACHING FROM MEMCACHED TO
REDIS AT 1.5M RPS WITHOUT DOWNTIME (6 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 Salesforce's Marketing Cloud team executed a zero-downtime migration
from Memcached to Redis Cluster, supporting 1.5 million cache events
per second for over 50 services under live production traffic. The
transition leveraged a Dynamic Cache Router, real-time routing,
compatibility layers for TTL and key handling, and hot-key detection
using a Count-Min Sketch model. End-to-end cache latency was
consistently maintained at P50 ≈ 1 ms and P99 ≈ 20 ms, ensuring
operational continuity. 

 FROM LOCAL TO GLOBAL: A DEEP DIVE INTO GRAPHRAG (8 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 GraphRAG enhances conventional RAG by building a hierarchical
knowledge graph from raw documents, enabling both granular local
retrieval and global corpus-level reasoning for LLMs. GraphRAG
synthesizes high-level insights and reduces hallucinations by using
token-overlapping chunking, entity resolution, weighted relationships,
and recursive community detection. The dual Local/Global retrieval
modes resolve prior trade-offs between precision and corpus-wide
understanding at the cost of pre-computation. 

 AUTOFILLING THE BORING SEMANTIC LAYER: FROM SAKILA TO CHAT-BI WITH
DLTHUB (12 MINUTE READ) [10] 

 Semantic layers should be simple, shared, and independent of any
single BI tool so the same definitions work for dashboards, APIs, and
AI. Using dlt for schema discovery, an LLM to draft the model, and a
“boring” semantic layer, most of the semantic work is automated
while keeping queries deterministic and debuggable. This enables
reliable Chat-BI and multi-modal analytics from one source of truth
without heavy infrastructure. 

 POWERING VECTOR EMBEDDING CAPABILITIES (6 MINUTE READ) [11] 

 Expedia Group developed a centralized Embedding Store by extending
the open-source Feast feature store with vector database capabilities,
enabling efficient creation, management, versioning, and querying of
vector embeddings for both real-time and batch workloads. This unified
system supports similarity and hybrid searches with metadata
filtering, and accelerates ML features like recommendations and
semantic search across the company. 

🚀 

OPINIONS & ADVICE

 CONTEXT IS THE NEXT DATA PLATFORM, AND WHY CONTEXT GRAPHS ARE KEY TO
UNDERSTANDING PROCESSES (5 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Context graphs help AI understand how work actually gets done by
capturing real processes, relationships, and activity across
enterprise tools, not just static data. By learning the repeated steps
and patterns of work, AI agents can automate tasks more reliably and
act in ways that match how an organization really operates. This makes
context graphs a core part of a new data platform built specifically
for agent-driven automation, not reporting. 

 DATA ENGINEERING IN 2026: WHAT CHANGES? (4 MINUTE READ) [13] 

 In the 2026 agent-native era, data engineering focuses on AI agents
as the primary "machine users," prioritizing automation, reliability,
and safety amid agents driving over 80% of new database creations and
surging prompt volumes. Key shifts include modular PARK (PyTorch, AI
Models, Ray, and Kubernetes) stacks, multimodal lakehouses, context
stores for business logic, confidence-gated execution for safety, and
ephemeral databases. 

 THE HIDDEN COST CRISIS IN DATA ENGINEERING (5 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Data engineering teams face escalating cloud infrastructure costs due
to unchecked tool sprawl, duplicated pipelines, and minimal cost
accountability, often leading engineers to spend up to 60% of their
time on maintenance instead of value-driving work. Implementing spend
attribution, creating centralized platform teams, formalizing data
contracts, and conducting regular audits have enabled organizations to
cut infrastructure spend by 40-60% within a quarter. 

💻 

LAUNCHES & TOOLS

 FIVETRAN KEEPS DATA PIPELINES FLOWING FOR TEAMS SHORT ON TIME AND
BANDWIDTH (SPONSOR) [15] 

 ⚡ Get your data where it needs to go — automatically. No
maintenance, no scripts, just fast, reliable data delivered from
source to destination, ready for analytics, reporting, and AI. With
Fivetran's 700+ fully managed connectors [15], you can start the year
with better pipelines — without adding to your workload.

👉 Try Fivetran for free today [15]

 DATABASES IN 2025: A YEAR IN REVIEW (8 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 In 2025, PostgreSQL dominated with version 18 enhancements, major
acquisitions (Databricks-Neon $1B and Snowflake-CrunchyData $250M),
emerging sharding projects, and deeper cloud integrations. Trends
included widespread Model Context Protocol (MCP) for LLM integration,
new columnar formats, DBMS failures, and waning GPU hype. 

 HOW MULTIMODAL VECTOR DATABASES ARE TRANSFORMING CHALLENGES ACROSS
INDUSTRIES (12 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Multimodal vector databases like ApertureDB natively handle diverse
data types in a unified system, offering semantic search, graph-based
relations, and full traceability for advanced cross-modal retrieval
and complex queries. They tackle healthcare compliance challenges by
automating the detection of regulatory omissions in drug
advertisements, leveraging tools such as Unstructured.io, GPT-4o, and
CLIP embeddings. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 MASTERING LLM TOOL CALLING: THE COMPLETE FRAMEWORK FOR CONNECTING
MODELS TO THE REAL WORLD (6 MINUTE READ) [18] 

 LLM tool calling is the mechanism enabling models to invoke external
functions/APIs, turning static LLMs into dynamic agents for data
access, computation, and real-world actions. It includes three pillars
to build reliable, production-ready agents: Data Access (retrieval
tools), Computation (precision processing), and Actions (effecting
changes). 

 HOW AI TRANSFORMED DATABASE DEBUGGING AT DATABRICKS (8 MINUTE READ)
[19] 

 Databricks developed an internal AI-powered agentic platform that
transforms database debugging for thousands of OLTP instances by
enabling conversational, natural-language interactions with unified
access to metrics, logs, and expert knowledge. This evolution from
rigid checklists and anomaly detection to an interactive multi-agent
system has reduced debugging time by up to 90%, allowing engineers to
resolve complex issues more efficiently. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 THE ADAPTIVE RETRIEVAL ADVANTAGE: WHY QUERY-AWARE RAG IS REPLACING
ONE-SIZE-FITS-ALL RETRIEVAL (10 MINUTE READ) [20] 

 Lightweight query classification slashes RAG costs and latency while
boosting precision for complex enterprise queries. 

 TRENDING: WHAT CONTEXT GRAPHS MEAN FOR ENTERPRISE (8 MINUTE READ)
[21] 

 Context graphs capture how work really happens, including the hidden
workflows and coordination that drive outcomes.

subject: Build your first app using AI. No coding required

Dear learner,

Many people have ideas for apps they wish existed, but still assume building them requires learning to code, installing tools, or waiting for someone else to make them real.

Today, we’re launching Build with Andrew (https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VW4D5f7_w4n3W1M4QdB84vrLtW1sXT7r5J0WyKN7zrx1j3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3mvW5gnNYG15bQv-W1-rLNb7lKlMpW7bnHj-3s5c3LW2P6gFW3KqjfFW5m1lkJ3-xyZ7W7XkTnH3FZ_vLW5fn4tm242kl3VMbWS-84vn-TW7KhHYL6RxhZ0VW3dCm2y8_5DW3kd8VQ9bHXs7W3jvbR_3DrNZPW119ybk2wFrzMVDRyJy3_sDlqW2hv1Hr2nHXMtW3bY9mL4mxjXmW8ClWCd7q37gTW93ftDs4QRyLHW1c5rd74cPdw7W2Gqh0H1RNLYxVbzz6Q2pvRHmW7dLyJZ338qZRW5sBBY27VJ78qW3LlBlV6tzcRMW4RQPbx8gRZmhVtdfZg8ljM4bdr_Y0j04 ) , a course designed to change that starting point.

In this course, Andrew Ng shows how to take an idea, describe it clearly in words, and use AI tools to turn it into a working web application—right away. No coding background is required. If you can explain what you want an app to do, you can build one.

You’ll begin by building a funny interactive birthday message generator that runs in your browser and can be shared with others. From there, you'll customize it by telling AI how you want it changed, tweaking it until it works exactly how you want.

By the end, you’ll have a repeatable framework you can use to build what you’d like – from fun projects to practical tools.

(https://info.deeplearning.ai/e3t/Ctc/LX+113/cJhC404/VW4D5f7_w4n3W1M4QdB84vrLtW1sXT7r5J0WyKN7zrx1j3prCCW7Y8-PT6lZ3mvW5gnNYG15bQv-W1-rLNb7lKlMpW7bnHj-3s5c3LW2P6gFW3KqjfFW5m1lkJ3-xyZ7W7XkTnH3FZ_vLW5fn4tm242kl3VMbWS-84vn-TW7KhHYL6RxhZ0VW3dCm2y8_5DW3kd8VQ9bHXs7W3jvbR_3DrNZPW119ybk2wFrzMVDRyJy3_sDlqW2hv1Hr2nHXMtW3bY9mL4mxjXmW8ClWCd7q37gTW93ftDs4QRyLHW1c5rd74cPdw7W2Gqh0H1RNLYxVbzz6Q2pvRHmW7dLyJZ338qZRW5sBBY27VJ78qW3LlBlV6tzcRMW4RQPbx8gRZmhVtdfZg8ljM4bdr_Y0j04 )

Along the way, you’ll learn how to:

- Build web applications by describing what you want to AI, with no coding needed
- Customize features like buttons, input fields, and color schemes
- Iterate confidently when outputs aren’t quite right
- Apply the same framework to build whatever you can imagine

If you’re already comfortable with AI or coding, you may recognize how powerful this shift is. Think of someone in your life who doesn't yet realize they can build things themselves, like your friends, parents, coworkers, or roommates who have ideas but think “building apps is too hard.”

This course is for them. Please share it!

body:
Elon Musk's xAI secured $20 billion in Series E funding. The company
plans to use the capital to scale its Grok
chatbot ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌  ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ ‌ 


 Sign Up [1] |Advertise [2]|View Online [3] 

		TLDR 

		TOGETHER WITH [Ring] [4]

TLDR AI 2026-01-07

 THE RING APPSTORE IS HERE! (SPONSOR) [4] 

 Ring just announced the Ring Appstore, opening the door for
developers to build Al-powered apps using Ring camera data [4]and
reach millions of users.

With Al-assisted tools, self-serve sandbox environments, and a
streamlined certification process, you have all the tools you need to
find new monetization path, iterate quickly, and distribute at a
massive scale.

Third-party developers are already building in beta. You can request
to join now, too.

👉 Request early access to the developer portal [4] to invent with
Ring

🚀 

HEADLINES & LAUNCHES

 XAI RAISES $20B (2 MINUTE READ) [5] 

 Elon Musk's xAI secured $20 billion in Series E funding from
investors including Nvidia, Fidelity, Cisco, and QIA. The company
plans to use the capital to scale its Grok chatbot and data center
infrastructure to serve its 600 million monthly active users. 

 DYNAMIC CONTEXT DISCOVERY IN CODING AGENTS (4 MINUTE READ) [6] 

 Cursor has introduced a token-efficient strategy called dynamic
context discovery where agents selectively pull relevant data during
inference rather than loading static context. Techniques include
treating tool outputs and terminal sessions as files, summarizing past
chat history, and selectively loading tools via the Agent Skills
standard. 

🧠 

DEEP DIVES & ANALYSIS

 BUILDING CONTEXT GRAPHS FOR GTM — AND WHY SALESFORCE CAN'T DO IT
(13 MINUTE READ) [7] 

 GTM is hard because context is fragmented across people and systems.
Salesforce may be a system of record, but it is not a source of truth
with comprehensive context and decision traces. One of the next
trillion-dollar opportunities in AI will come from systems that
capture decision traces, not just data. These context graphs will
capture how things happened - what decisions were made, what changed,
and why an account moved the way it did. 

 DATABASE DEVELOPMENT WITH AI IN 2026 (7 MINUTE READ) [8] 

 In 2026, AI will significantly impact database development by
assisting with routine reporting queries and schema generation for new
applications. Stable SQL language aids AI in this. However, poorly
documented existing databases and the need for precision in critical
tasks present challenges. AI adoption will flourish in new projects,
but legacy systems will still demand human involvement due to
complexities and inadequate tooling. 

🧑‍💻 

ENGINEERING & RESEARCH

 AI GATEWAY SUPPORT FOR CLAUDE CODE (1 MINUTE READ) [9] 

 Vercel AI Gateway's Anthropic-compatible API endpoint now features
Claude Code. Developers can now route Claude Code requests through AI
Gateway to centralize usage and spend, view traces in observability,
and benefit from failover between providers. Users will have to log
out and back in and set environment variables to configure Claude Code
to use AI Gateway. 

 CLAUDE BOOTSTRAP (GITHUB REPO) [10] 

 AI can generate infinite code, but humans are still needed to review,
understand, and maintain it. This moves the bottleneck from code
generation to code comprehension. Claude Bootstrap is an opinionated
project initialization system for Claude Code. It keeps AI-generated
code simple, secure, and verifiable. 

 AI OBSERVER (GITHUB REPO) [11] 

 AI Observer is a self-hosted, single-binary, OpenTelemetry-compatible
observability backend designed to monitor local AI coding tools. It
can track token usage, cost, API latency, error rates, and session
activity across all AI coding assistants on a unified dashboard. AI
Observer features multi-tool support, a real-time dashboard,
customizable widgets, and more. Screenshots are available in the
repository. 

 FALCON-H1R: REASONING WITH A 7B MODEL (38 MINUTE READ) [12] 

 Falcon-H1R is a 7B model optimized for reasoning tasks, rivaling
models up to 7× larger in benchmark performance. Through efficient
training and architecture, it improves token usage, inference speed,
and Chain-of-Thought capabilities. 

🎁 

MISCELLANEOUS

 AI LEADERBOARD MAKER LMARENA HITS $1.7 BILLION VALUATION (1 MINUTE
READ) [13] 

 LMArena has raised a $150 million series A fundraising round at a
valuation of $1.7 billion. The startup has raised $250 million in the
last seven months. Its leaderboard started as a research project that
showed the results of human evaluations of AI models for various
tasks. The public laiderboard is now a hotly contested proving ground
for new models. 

 AI NEEDS GAME DESIGNERS (7 MINUTE READ) [14] 

 Game designers have spent decades figuring out how to let humans
direct complex, multi-agent systems in real-time, surface information
at the right moment, and make something intricate feel intuitive. The
command interfaces in RTS games are the result of decades of iteration
on parallel attention management. Someone needs to build an interface
for AI agents that allows users to spin up workers, assign them to
control groups, see their status on a dashboard, get alerts when they
need attention, and coordinate their work. The people most suited to
build this are game designers. 

⚡ 

QUICK LINKS

 THE SUBTLE VOICEBUDS USE AI TO TRANSCRIBE YOUR WORDS BELOW A WHISPER,
OR IN VERY LOUD SPACES (3 MINUTE READ) [15] 

 Subtle's Voicebuds use AI to transcribe speech below a whisper or in
loud environments, reducing transcription errors by five times
compared to AirPods Pro 3. 

 ALIEN PROCESSES, DOMAINS, AND DATA MODELS (4 MINUTE READ) [16] 

 AI agents will profoundly transform business processes, domains, and
data models, making them seem alien-like. 

 GOOGLE BIG SLEEP: LINUX VULNERABILITIES (1 MINUTE READ) [17] 

 Google Big Sleep has published the reports for BIGSLEEP-458654612,
BIGSLEEP-462435176, and BIGSLEEP-463332873. 

 WRAPPING MY HEAD AROUND GAS TOWN (7 MINUTE READ) [18]
